text: - All F1, F2 and F3 Contacts of an RT-PCR confirmed positive case shall undergo mandatory RT-PCR Testing. The date of testing shall be determined by the Contact Tracing Team, or the District Health Office. If the RT-PCR result of an F1 Contact is positive, all F2 contacts will be elevated to Fl Contacts. There shall be free COVID-l9 RT-PCR Testing for all Ft, F2, and F3 Contacts at Swab Centers duly authorized by the Davao City Health Office (CHO). All asymptomatic individuals shall undergo mandatory RT-PCR Testing not earlier that the fifth day immediately after the date of the last exposure. All close contacts who have been traced beyond the seventh (Zth) day from his/her last exposure and who remained asymptomatic shall no longer undergo mandatory RT-PCR Testing.

text: - The following protocols for close contacts of probable, suspect, and confirmed COVID-19 cases shall hereinafter be obserued: Ord. No. 0778-2L 1. All FO's, irrespective of whether they are fully or paftially vaccinated, shall immediately undergo foufteen (14) days mandatory isolation or as determined by the attending physician in accordance with the Omnibus Guidelines on Prevention, Detection, Isolation, Treatment, and Reintegration (PDTTR). 2. Fully Vaccinated Individuals who are F1 Close Contacts shall undergo a shortened 7-day mandatory quarantine provided his/her RT-PCR yielded a negative result and that he/she remains asymptomatic for the entire duration of the 7-day period. The first day being the date immediately after the last day of exposure. Should the RT-PCR Test yield a positive result or he/she becomes asymptmatic, he/she shall follow the prescribed isolation protocols as provided by the current DOH Omnibus Guidelines on Minimum Public Health Standards and the IATF Resolutions. 3. Paftially Vaccinated Individuals or Unvaccinated individuals who are F1 Close Contacts shall undergo the prescribed mandatory quarantine period as provided by the DOH Omnibus Guidelines on Minimum Public Health Standards and the IATF Resolutions. 4. All F2 and F3 Close Contacts need not undergo mandatory quarantine provided that they do not exhibit Influenza-Like-Illness (IU). All F2 and F3 Contacts shall be advised to self-monitor, strictly adhere to the minimum health standards, and repoft for appearance of signs or symptoms. SECTION T. . AII FO, F1, and F2 Contacts shall disclose their close contacts including their contact number and home/work address.

text: POLICY STATEMENT - One of the State Policies as provided for in the Constitution is for the State to protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them. In its vision to have a country with well informed, empowered, responsible and healthy adolescents who are leaders in the society, the Depaftment of Health also has the Adolescent Health and Development Program, with the objective to improve the health status of adolescents and enable them to fully enjoy their rights to health. As such, all adolescents should have access to comprehensive health care and services in an adolescent-friendly environment. The Philippines also adheres to the United Nations Convention on the Right of the Child which provides for the right of the child to the enjoyment of the highest attainable standard of health and to facilities for the treatment of illness and rehabilitation of health and for their right of access to such health care seruices. Davao City also provides in its Davao City Women's Health Care Ordinance in 2013 that the rights and welfare of adolescents must also be protected. Thus, it is the policy of the City Government of Davao to provide healthcare seruices to its constituents, particularly to the vulnerable sectors of the society, such as the teens/adolescents, in line with its mandate as a Iocal government unit to promote the general welfare and the health and safety of its constituents.

text: PURPOSE - This Ordinance aims to establish a Youth and Adolescent Center in the City of Davao, which will answer to the needs of the youth and adolescents, such as in matters of reproductive and mental health. It will serue as a core or specific referral point that provides youth and adolescents with access to holistic healthcare and other seruices. The composite objectives of the Youth and Adolescent Center are as follows: (1) To create awareness among the youth and adolescents on reproductive health, gender equality and mental health; (2) To create a youth and adolescent-friendly avenue where health services, including that of mental health seryices, are accessible, acceptable, equitable, appropriate and effective; (3) To respond to the various health and psychosocialconditions of youths and adolescents; (4) To conduct trainings for healthcare personnel on how to properly deal with the youth and adolescents; (5) To empower young men and women through the programs of Service Delivery, Youth and Adolescent Hotline, Community Outreach, lnformation Education Communication, Training and Research. t Page 3 of L2 Ord. text: - It is hereby declared as poliry of the City of Davao that the valiant contributions given by war veterans in times of war must be given due recognition. While their bodies have aged, they are exemplars of patriotism and self-sacrifice. Therefore, when their heroic voices are ultimately silenced by death, the City of Davao take upon itself the duty of providing financial assistance to their families for a dignified burial.
title: AN ORDINANCE GRANTIilG BURIAL ASSISTANCE TO WORLD WAR II VETERANS IN THE AMOUNT oF TEN THOUSAilD PESOS (P10,000)" TO *DAVAO CITY VETERANS WELFARE AND VETERANS PROGRAM" AND GRANTING AN INCREASE IN THE BURIAL ASSISTANCE, AND TO REDUCE REQUTREMENTS FOR CTATMTNG SUCH ASSISTANCE I

text: DEFINffiON OF TERMS- The following terms are hereby defined for the purpose of this Ordinance , to wit, (a) Veterans - shal! include any person or persons who served in the regularly constituted air, !and, or naval services or arms, or in such non-regularly organized military units in the Philippines during World War II, Korean War and Veteran's of Military Campaign and whose seruices with such units are duly recognized by the Republic of the Philippines or by the Government of the United States: Provided, that for purposes of this Ordinance, the term \eteran or veterans" also include the widow, oryhan or a compulsory heir of a deceased veteran, as determined by existing laws; (b) Children - shall refer to the sons and/or daughters of the deceased veterans by blood, legitimate or illegitimate, and to his children by fiction of law, such as by adoption (c) Spouse - shall mean the wife of the veteran under a valid marriage; (d) Relative- shall mean a member of the family of the veteran within the 5th civil degree of consanguinity (e) Entitled Heir - shall mean the heir ultimately entitled to the financial burial assistance, determined after applying the rules for entitlement as hereinafter provided
title: AN ORDINANCE GRANTIilG BURIAL ASSISTANCE TO WORLD WAR II VETERANS IN THE AMOUNT oF TEN THOUSAilD PESOS (P10,000)" TO *DAVAO CITY VETERANS WELFARE AND VETERANS PROGRAM" AND GRANTING AN INCREASE IN THE BURIAL ASSISTANCE, AND TO REDUCE REQUTREMENTS FOR CTATMTNG SUCH ASSISTANCE I

text: FINANCIAL BURIAL ASSISTANCE - Upon the death, the heir of a veteran shall be entitled to a financial burial assistance of Twenty Thousand Pesos (P20,000) upon compliance of the requirements hereinafter provided in this Ordinance.

text: @ - The deceased veteran's surviving spouse, children and nearest suliving relatives by consanguinity shall be entitled to the financial burial assistance which shall be claimed once.
title: AN ORDINANCE GRANTIilG BURIAL ASSISTANCE TO WORLD WAR II VETERANS IN THE AMOUNT oF TEN THOUSAilD PESOS (P10,000)" TO *DAVAO CITY VETERANS WELFARE AND VETERANS PROGRAM" AND GRANTING AN INCREASE IN THE BURIAL ASSISTANCE, AND TO REDUCE REQUTREMENTS FOR CTATMTNG SUCH ASSISTANCE I

text: RUTES FOR EilTITLEMEilT TO CIAIM - The following rules shall be obserued in determining the entitled heir, to wit, a. The heirs shall be entitled to the financial burial assistance in the order they appear in SECTION 5 thereof; b. The deceased veteran's children or relative cannot receive the burial assistance if the surviving spouse comes forward to claim the same. Hence, a claim by the deceased veteran's suriving spouse shall exclude claims by his children and relatives. The suryiving spouse shall be deemed an entitled heir only upon due presentation of their marriage certificate; Ord. No. 0818-21 c. If the veteran's spouse had predeceased him, a claim by his children shall exclude claims by his relatives. Among the children, priority shall be given to the child with whom the veteran last resided or to the eldest child. To be deemed an entitled heir, the filiation or relationship of the child or relative to the veterans may be proven by the presentation of birth certificates.

CVAO ceftification or Barangay Clearance, to prove that the deceased veteran was a resident of Davao City for at least five (5) years, counted from the time of his death.

KTV establishment - a commercial establishment that offers enclosed and sound-proofed rooms for videoke machines for a fee.

text: DECLARATION OF POLICIES OF THE CITY GOVERNMENT OF DAVAO - It shal! be the policy of the Local Government of Davao City to uphold and value the dignity of every human person and guarantee full respect for human rights. Consistent with the UN Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW), Republic Act No. 97L0, or the Magna Carta of Women's Rights and Republic Act No. 11313, or the Safe Spaces Act, it is likewise the policy of the City Government of Davao to guarantee the equality of men and women so they may enjoy the full beneflts of development free and safe from all forms of gender-based harassment, not only in private but also in public spaces and online spaces. text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - As used in this Ordinance, the following terms are defined as follows: (a) (b) Act refers to Republic Act No. 11313, or the "safe Spaces Act". (c) Catcalling refers to unwanted remarks directed towards a person, commonly done in the form of wolf-whistling and misogynistic, transphobic, homophobic and sexist slurs. (d) Common carriers refer to persons, corporations, firms or associations engaged in the business of carrying or transporting passengers or goods or both, by land, water, or air, for compensation, offering their seruices to the public. (e) cyberstalking is a form of stalking that is committed through an electronic medium in which online communication takes place. text: ACTS OF GENDER.BASED SEXUAL HARASSMENT - The offenses of gender-based sexual harassment are committed through any unwanted, unsolicited, unwelcomed actions of a sexual nature or remarks referring to a person's sex, gender and/or sexuality, regardless of the motive for committing such action or remarks, provided fufther that, the positions, hierarchy and stature of the perpetrator and victim shall not matter in considering the act as gender-based sexual harassment. It may include the following, among others: a. Catcalling, wolf-whistling, unwanted invitations, misogynistic, transphobic, homophobic, and sexist slurs; b. Persistent uninvited comments or gestures on a person's appearance; c. Relentless requests for personal details; d. Statement of sexual comments and suggestions; e. Public masturbation or flashing of private pafts, groping, making offensive body gestures at someone, and other similar lewd sexua! actions; f. Any advances, whether verbal or physical, that is unwanted and has threatened one's sense of personal space and physical safety. This may include cursing, leering and intrusive gazing, and taunting; g. Persistent telling of sexual jokes, use of sexual names; and h. Stalking. It may also be committed through online spaces using information and communications technology by harassing, intimidating or threatening the victim through: a) Physical, psychological, and emotional threats, unwanted sexual misogynistic, transphobic, homophobic and sexist remarks and comments online whether publicly or through direct and private messages; b) Invasion of the victim's privary through ryberstalking and incessant messaging; c) Uploading and sharing without the consent of the victim any form of media that contains photos, voice, or video with sexual content; d) Any unauthorized recording and sharing of any of the victim's photos, videos or any information online; e) Impersonating identities of victims online or posting lies about victims to harm their reputation; or f) Filing false abuse repofts to online platforms to silence victims. text: DECLARATION OF POUCY - The fight against COVID-19 requires a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach. The shared responsibility of national government agencies, local government units, various sectors of society, especially communities and individuals, is a necessary exercise to prevent the transmission of the virus. While vaccine is among the solutions, it is not the only solution to end the pandemic. Continued adherence to minimum public health standards, effective surueillance and disease management as well as capability-building to weather future public health emergencies is a must. It is hereby declared a policy of the State to take a proactive role in the health care of its citizens. Towards this end, the State shall adopt a comprehensive immunization program for COVID-19 in Davao City (thereafter known as the "Program") which shall cover all its residents, ensuring that the promise of normalization of everyday life is achieved.

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - The terms used in this Ordinance are herein defined as follows: a) Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI)- any untoward medical occurrence which follows immunization and which does not necessarily have a causal relationship with the usage of the vaccine. The adverse event may be any unfavorable or unintended sign, abnormal laboratory finding, symptom or disease. b) Adverse Events of Special Interest (AESI)- a pre-identifled and predetermined medically-significant event that has the potential to be causally associated with a vaccine product that needs to be carefully monitored and confirmed by fufther specific studies. c) Ancillary immunization supplies - supplies other than the vaccine itself, which is used to administer the vaccine, and includes Personal Protective Equipment (PPEs), autodisabled needles and syringes, mixing syringes, Safety Collector Boxes (SCB), and others. d) Cold chain management - is a logistics management process for vaccines that require refrigerated temperatures. It involves performing a chain of tasks to prepare, store, and transport products along the cold supply chain. Failure to keep vaccines under the required cold conditions will render them unusable, leading to spoilage and wastage. For COVID-l9 vaccines, required refrigeration ranges from +Boc to as low as -B0oc. e) Coronavirus (COVID-19) - a large family of viruses causing a range of illnesses, from the common cold to more serious infections such as those caused by Middle East Respiratory Syndrome-related Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome-related Coronavirus (SARS-CoV). In 2019, the appearance of a new strain of coronavirus that has not been previously identified in humans was recorded. On 12 February 2020, the World Health Organization (WHO) announced that the novel disease is officially called Coronavirus Disease 19 or COVID-19, and the virus infecting it is referred to as COVID-19 virus. 0 COVID-19 vaccine - a vaccine intended to provide acquired imrnunity against covrD-19. Ord. Ncr. 0478-2L g) Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) - a mechanism to facilitate the availability and use of medical counter measures, including vaccines, during public health emergencies, such as the current COVID-19 pandemic. Under the EUA, the Philippine Food and Drug Administration (FDA) may allow the use of unapproved medica! products, or unapproved uses of approved medical products in an emergency to diagnose, treat, or prevent serious or life-threatening diseases or conditions when certain statutory criteria under FDA Circular No. 2020-036 have been met, considering that there are no adequate, approved, and available alternatives. h) Herd immunity - a form of indirect protection from infectious disease that occurs when a sufficient percentage of a population has become immune to an infection, whether through vaccination or previous infections, thereby reducing the likelihood of infection for individuals who lack immunity. i) Immunization - The process by which an individual's immune system becomes fortified against an agent (or antigen), most commonly gained through vaccination. Also terms used interchangeably with immunization: "inoculation" and "vaccination." This means the use of vaccine-induced immunity in a person against a vaccine-preventable disease. j) Informed consent - permission granted in the knowledge of the possible consequences, typically that which is given by a patient to a doctor/medical practitioner for treatment/interuention with full knowledge of the possible risks and benefits. k) Pandemic - an epidemic occurring worldwide, or over a very wide area, crossing international boundaries and usually affecting a large number of people. The classical definition includes nothing about population immunity, virology or disease severity. l) Vaccines - biological preparations which stimulate the body's own immune system to protect the person against subsequent infection or disease. Vaccines as defined in this Ordinance shall be limited to those produced against COVID-19. m) Vulnerable groups/population - refers to, but is not limited to those who are incapable of protecting their own interests such as pregnant women, neonates, children, fetuses, prisoners, physically handicapped, mentally challenged, economically disadvantaged, institutionalized and very sick patients, etc.

text: FORMULATION OF A COMMUNITY-BASED COVID-l9 IMMUNIZATION PLAN. The City of Davao shall follow a community-based framework in executing the Program.This framework shall treat barangays and other community subsets as active paftners in program execution in order to ensure thorough immunization coverage of persons, adequate and equitable access to the vaccine, and proper postimmunization attention and monitoring. The City Health Office (CHO) and the Depaftment of Health Center for Health Development Davao (DOH-CHD Davao) shall create this framework with input from other frontline agencies. Fufthermore, as the Program requires a whole-of-society approach, pafticipating agencies and the private sector are also enjoined to closely coordinate with the local government in the implementation of the Program. sEcTIoN7.@-TheCHoshallbetheleadagencyinthe implementation of the COVID-19 immunization program. It shall identiff and train health workers for the purpose of vaccine handling, storage and administration, as well as other aspects of the Program. All vaccinators should be adequately trained. No immunization shall be performed by untrained/uncertified/unauthorized personnel. Any unauthorized administering of vaccine shall be punishable by this Ordinance and other applicable laws. The COVID-l9 Electronic Immunization Registry (CEIR) shall be the official platform for masterlisting and registration for COVID-19 vaccination. All health facilities (hospitals, vaccination centers, etc.) within the city shall submit its own masterlist through the CEIR, which will be consolidated by the CHO, who shall ensure that there will be no duplication in masterlists across facilities within their catchment. Every person vaccinated under this Ordinance shall be given an immunization card which shall reflect the date of immunization, the immunization round/dose received, and other peftinent details. This same data shall also be recorded in the CEIR. Proof of vaccination and subsequent receipt of immunization card shall not mean exemption from continued strict obseruance of basic health protocols. The identity of the person vaccinated and other required information shall be recorded and kept by the CHO for documentation, archiving and other similar purposes. Information shall also be used for other post-immunization concerns but shall remain private and confidential. In this regard, an efficient method of record-keeping shall be developed which shall ensure a streamlined delivery of the vaccine and detailed record-keeping of persons vaccinated and doses administered. Informed consent form shall be distributed in Program areas, and no person shall be vaccinated without first submitting a duly-accomplished informed consent form. Since specific COVID-19 vaccine types may require multiple doses to achieve full efficiency and effectivity, multiple immunization rounds may be implemented, thus the need for careful record-keeping and documentation. Persons thus vaccinated are required to be given the full vaccine regimen (multiple doses as required by the manufacturer) for full effect.

CHD Davao and the Local Government shall develop a distribution plan appropriate to the specific requirements in its jurisdiction, which shall be consolidated by the National COVID-19 Task Force in order to come up with a comprehensive national cold chain and logistics plan for COVID-19 immunization.

text: VACCINE PRIORITIZATION AND PRIORIW ELIGIBLE GROUPS - The implementation of actual immunization shall be in phases, depending on the delivery (timing, available doses, logistica! requirements) of vaccines to the country. Deployment shall be based on a sectora! approach within each priority group. As much as possible, the guidelines in the Philippine National Deployment and Vaccination Plan for COVID-19 Vaccines shall be followed, to wit: I. Priority Eligible Group A a. Frontline health workers from the private and public sector currently on active practice/seruice, regardless if permanent, contractual, job-order, and/or outsourced employees or staff; b. Indigent Senior Citizens registered and as determined by the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD); c. Remaining Senior Citizens - ALL senior citizens (not categorized as indigent) registered and as determined by DSWD; d. Remaining Indigent Population as determined by DSWD; e. All enlisted uniformed personnel in active seruice under the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), Philippine National Police (PNP), Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) and the Citizen Armed Force Geographical Unit (CAFGU), II. Priority Eligible Group B a. All teachers and school workers, whether permanent, job-order, contractual or outsourced in all educational levels, from primary, secondary, teftiary, and vocational educational institutions, both private and public; b. All government workers, whether permanent, job-order, contractual or outsourced, in national government agencies, Government-Owned and Controlled Corporations (GOCCS), Government Financial Institutions (GFIs), local government units, among others; Ord. No. 0478-21 c. Essential workers, including all those coming from the sectors of agriculture, forestry and flsheries; transportation; construction; food industries; manufacturing of essential goods; tourism; essential retail; water-refilling stations; laundry seruices; logistics seruice providers; delivery and courier seruices; water supply and sanitation seruices; telecommunication seruices; energy and power companies; gasoline stations, among others; and those similarly providing basic seruices during the time of pandemic and essential to the growth of the economy as determined by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) and the Depaftment of Labor and Employment (DOLE); d. Socio-demographic groups at significant higher risk other than senior citizens and indigent populations (e.9. Persons Deprived of Libefi (PDLs), Persons with Disabilities (PWDs), Indigenous Peoples, Filipinos living in high-density areas; e. Eligible students in primary, secondary, teftiary, and vocational educationa! institutions, upon the recommendations of the World Health Organization (WHO) and the National Immunization Technical Advisory Group (NffAG); f. Filipino migrant workers who reside in another country for a limited period of employment that were not vaccinated; g. All remaining Filipino workforce as determined by DOLE, DTI and Civil Seruice Commission (CSC); III. Priority Eligible Group C a. All remaining Filipino citizens not mentioned in Groups A and B These priority groups may be subject to other considerations based on the latest developments and scientific evidence and may be revised as reflected in the Philippine COVID-19 National Vaccine Deployment Plan. For purposes of herd immunity, the Immunization Program shall continue to run until at least 70 to 85 percent of the population in the City is immunized. Within the City, the deployment of vaccines to specific areas, districts, and barangdys, shall be based on the burden of COVID-19 cases, using the indicators as defined by NITAG, to wit: a. number of active cases in recent four (4) weeks b. attack rate per 100,000 in recent four (4) weeks

text: CREATION OF A LOCAL ADVERSE EVENTS FOLLOWING rMt4uNrzATroN (AEFr) COMMTTTEE SPECTFTC TO COVIp-19 IMMUNIZATION - A local AEFI Committee shall be created, whose role is to respond to any adverse events following immunization through repofting, monitoring, surueillance, cross-agency collaboration, and other coordinated modes. The composition of the AEFI/AESI Committee shall be taken from the following fields of expertise: 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. Pediatrics Neurology Vi rology/Microbiology Epidemiology Immunology Forensic Pathology Other medical expefts (as necessary), may include a. Geriatrics b. Adult Medicine c. Infectious disease Membership shall be subject to a Non-Disclosure and Confidentiality Agreement The roles and functions of the AEFI/AESI committee are as follows: 1. Review all reported serious and cluster of minor AEFI cases presented for expert opinion and provide the flnal causality assessment of the AEFI cases. The National AEFI Committee will provide the final causality of AEFI cases including those that were not classifled by the Regional AEFI Committee. 2. Ensure evidence-based causality assessment by recommending fufther investigation and data collection as needed. 3. Make final decisions on causality assessment of inconclusive investigations. 4. Ensure that standard protocols for AEFI surueillance and investigation are correctly followed, 5. Engage with other national expefts when requirements arise in establishing causality and vaccine quality issues. 6. Provide recommendations to the CHO and DOH XI, Epidemiology Bureau, and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on improving immunization service delivery, compliance with injection safety and effective vaccine management based on lessons from the AEFI cases. 7. Serue as technical advisory group to the CHO on vaccine and immunization safety-related issue(s) of highest consideration including immediate recall of vaccine and/or temporary/permanent withdrawal of a vaccine from the immunization program. Ord. No. 0478-27 B. Serue as resource person in other AEFI related meetings, conferences or capacity-building activities as requested. While all relevant documents, data and records may be shared and reviewed among other AEFI/AESI committees and the National Adverse Events Following Immunization Committee (NAEFIC) for assessment, evaluation, and other purposes, information gathered is protected against public disclosure by RA 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 20t2. Public statements about the causality assessment, especially relating to AEFI/AESI deaths may be made as long as confidentiality is maintained. All other details not covered in this SECTION shall be supplied by the prevailing AEFI/AESI guidelines in force. AEFI cases under the jurisdiction of the committee shall not only be restricted to those connected with the Program but shall also include AEFI from other COVID immunization avenues.

text: PURPOSE AND INTENT - The enactment of this Ordinance is anchored upon the primary purpose of promoting the interest and welfare of the people of Davao City by integrating urban canopy in the City's public streets, highways, parks and playgrounds. The planet faces a climate crisis due to various reasons. This is manifested through increasing temperature, rising sea levels due to rapidly melting polar ice caps and glaciers, frequent forest fires and droughts, to name a few. Climate change poses a threat, of which even the City does not have immunity. In response, the trees will contribute to the measures the City is taking to al[eviate the detrimental effects caused by global warming and maintaining its status as an eco-friendly City. These treelines are also in support of the City's urbanization as this will benefit all drivers who often cruise during the day in the heat, the commuting public who usually walk to anive at their destinations, and the people who seek to spend their leisure time in parks and playgrounds. Ultimately, the Iegislative intent of the Ordinance focuses on making the City more conducive to environmental growth and protection, serving the purpose of promoting the welfare and interest of the people. text: DEFINITION OF TERMS a. African Swine Fever (ASF) - is a highly contagious hemorrhagic viral disease of domestic and wild pigs, which is responsible for serious economic and production losses. b. ASF affected areas - defined as areas within or outside the territorial jurisdiction of the Republic of the Philippines declared by the proper Government bodies as having tested positive for ASF virus using the recommended laboratory test. c. Biosecurity - refers to measures aimed at preventing the introduction and/or spread of harmful organisms (e.9. viruses, bacteria, etc.) to animals and plants in order to minimize the risk of transmission of infectious diseases. d. Boar semen - Boar semen is a suspension of sperm cells and secretions from the boar reproductive tract, including the accessory glands. The fluid portion of this suspension is known as seminal plasma and it helps to carry and protect the sperm cells. In boars, the semen also contains large quantities of gel. e. Carcass - the carcass of an animal, including part of the carcass and the meat, bones, hide, skin, hoofs, horns, wool, offal and other pafts of an animal. f . Cold storage facility - an installation intended for the cooling, freezing, and cold storage of perishable food products and other perishables. g. Exhibition sale - a public display of goods for sale, exchange, barter or trade, whether for profit or not. h. Good Animal Husbandry Practices (GAHP) - it is a set of principles of good practices and minimum requirements for the commercial/ backyard rearing/ farming of animals for food use. Ord. No. 0528-21 i. OIE - Office International des Epizooties or the World Organization for Animal Health. It is an international organization responsible for improving animal health worldwide. j. Pork - the meat of pig that is used for food, either whole carcass, fabricated or in the form of retail or choice cuts, whether fresh, processed, cooked, refrigerated or frozen. k. Pork by-products - are fresh, frozen, processed or cooked products derived and/or processed from pork, whether cooked or uncooked, that includes alpha (pork fat), bacon, sausages, chorizo, tocino, hotdogs, corned pork, ham and the like. It also includes marinated or ready-to-cook pork meat, canned pork, and pork-based sauces intended for human consumption. l. Sale or distribution - any form of sale, conveyance or transfer of ownership of meat or its by-products. It may include sale or generous transfer of pork and/or its by-products from the owner, broker, store owner, stall owner, mall, or its agents or representatives to the recipient or third party. This also includes selling by means of internet or through online-selling. m. Swill feeding - is the traditional name for the feeding of food scraps to pigs. n. Unsold or excess order - the difference between the quantity of pork and its byproducts withdrawn from the cold storage facility over the quantity displayed, sold, used for processing and manufactured outside the cold storage facility by the owner, vendor, seller, manufacturer or supplier. text: REGULATIONS ON SWILL FEEDING A. For swine raisers: 1. Practice strict biosecurity and good animal husbandry practices in respective farms; 2. Prohibit feeding raw/swill or food wastes ("lamaw") to pigs, unless the raw/swill or food wastes is treated with proper heating or preparation method under "2019 OIE Terrestrial Animal Health Code". (Temperature of at least 90 t for at least 60 minutes and continuous stirring) B. The table left-overs or food wastes/swill ("lamaw") shall be properly prepared or heated using the abovementioned method prior to disposal, sale or transfer to swine raisers. C. For all other concerned agencies and barangay officials in their respective jurisdiction: 1. Conduct information, education, and communication activities on ASF prevention especially the prohibition on swill/food wastes ("lamaw") feeding. 2. Conduct regular monitoring of health status of swine. 3. Ensure that illegal market products (fresh, frozen or processed) are not being sold in the market. 4. text: DECLARATION OF POLICY - It is the policy of the State to adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development which shall endeavor to make essential goods, health and other social seruices available to all people at affordable cost. To carry out the above policy, a City Hospital is to be established to fufther cater to the needs of the fast-growing populace, and to reduce the dependence on the Southern Philippines Medical Center as the sole government-operated teftiary care facility within the City. The creation of the hospital also serves as the City's response to the COVID-19 pandemic as well as future outbreaks, and will provide the City with the needed manpower, facility, and experience to counter such threats in the future.

As a government owned 100-bed Level III Training Hospital, and as a COVID-19 response, the Davao City Hospital, shall provide seryices for all kinds of illnesses, diseases, injuries or deformities. Dental Clinic, Neonatal Intensive Care Unit, Dialysis Clinic B. As to Ancillary Seryices o Tertiary Clinical Laboratory with Histopathology; . Blood Bank; . 3'd level X-ray o pharmacy Ord. text: . - As used in this Ordinance, the terms below shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this SECTION and as defined in the Labor Code. Any words or terms not defined shall be given their plain and customary meanings, unless the context requires otherwise, and shall be interpreted in a manner consistent with the purpose and spirit of this Ordinance. 1. Worker - means any member of the labor force, whether employed or unemployed. 2. Handicapped Workers - are those whose earning capacity is impaired by age or physical or mental deficiency or injury. 3. Employee - includes any person in the employ of an employer. The term shall not be limited to the employees of a pafticular employer, unless the Labor Code so explicitly states. It shall include any individual whose work has ceased as a result of or in connection with any current labor dispute or because of any unfair labor practice if he has not obtained any other substantially equivalent and regular employment. It refers to a person in the seruice of another under any contract of hire, express or implied, oral or written, where the employer has the power or right to control and direct the employee in the material details of how the work is to be performed. 4. Overseas Filipino Workers - refers to any person who is a documented worker and receiving compensation for such works outside of the Philippines while in the seruice of an employer in a state of which he or she is not a legal residenU to be used interchangeably with migrant workers or OFWs, as defined under Republic Act No. 8042 or the Migrant Workers Act of 1995, as amended by Republic Act No. 10022 or An Act Amending Republic Act. No. 8042, or any other applicable laws for overseas workers, (taken from the OFW Families Welfare and Crisis Center Ordinance of Davao City). 5. Solo Parent - any individua! who falls under any of the following categories: (1) A woman who gives bifth as a result of rape and other crimes against chastity even without a final conviction of the offender: Provided, that the mother keeps and raises the child; that: Ord. No. 0585-21 (3) Parent left solo or alone with responsibility of parenthood while the spouse is detained or is seruing sentence for a criminal conviction for at least one (1) year; (4) Parent left solo or alone with the responsibility of parenthood due to physical and/or mental incapacity of spouse as ceftified by a public medical practitioner; (5) Parent left solo or alone with the responsibility of parenthood due to legal separation or de fado separation from spouse for at least one (1) year, as long as he/she is entrusted with the custody of the children; (6) Parent left solo or alone with the responsibility of parenthood due declaration of nullity of annulment of marriage as decreed by a couft or by a church as long as he/she is entrusted with the custody of the children; (7) Parent left solo or alone with the responsibility of parenthood due to abandonment of spouse for at least one (1) year; (8) Unmarried mother/father who has preferred to keep and rear her/his child/children instead of having others care for them or give them up to a welfare institution; (9) Any person who solely provides parental care and suppoft to a child or children; (10) Any family member who assumes the responsibility of head of family as a result of the death, abandonment, disappearance or prolonged absence of the parents or solo parent. A change in the status of circumstance of the parent claiming benefits under this Act, such that he/she is no longer left alone with the responsibility of parenthood, shall terminate his/her eligibility for these benefits. ( Solo Parents'Welfare Act of 2000.') 6. Women in the enteftainment industry - as minimum wage earner, not included in raid, to be rescued and not discriminated. Seats for women workers - pregnant, separate toilet, breastfeeding workers (see Women's Development Code of the City) 7. Senior citizen or elderly - refers to any resident citizen of the Philippines at least sixty (60) years old (Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 2010). B. Persons with Disability - are those who have long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which in their interaction with various barriers may hinder their full and effective pafticipation in society on an equal basis with others. 9. Contractual employee - includes one employed by a contractor or subcontractor to perform or complete a job, work or seruice, pursuant to an arrangement between the latter and a principal. (2) Parent left solo or alone with the responsibility of parenthood due to the death of spouse. Ord. No. 0585-21 10. Barangay Workers - these include Barangay officials and members who may be designated by law or ordinance and charged with the maintenance of public order, protection and security of life and property, or the maintenance of a desirable and balanced environment of the Barangay. ll.Employer - includes any person acting in the interest of an employer, directly or indirectly. The term shall not include any labor organization or any of its officers or agents except when acting as an employer. It also refers to a person or organization that hires people to perform work in exchange for compensation, which is usually money in the form of wages or salary. Most countries have legislation governing relationships between employers and the people they hire, setting out the rights and responsibilities of each. 12. Construction Workers - those who are employed in the construction industry and its subdivisions, namely: general building construction, general engineering construction, and special trade construction, based on the classification code of the Philippine Accreditation Board of Construction Industry Authority of the Philippines; to companies and entities involved in demolition works; and to those falling within the construction industry as determined by the Secretary of Labor and Employment. 13. BPO Workers - those who are employed in a central customer seruice where agents or customer care specialists or customer seruice representatives handle business-related telephone calls (or e-mail) and other IT-related activities on behalf of a client. 14. Labor Organizations - means any union or association of employees which exists in whole or in paft for the purpose of collective bargaining or of dealing with employers concerning terms and conditions of employment. 15. Labor or Industrial Dispute - includes any controversy or matter concerning terms or conditions of employment or the association or representation of persons in negotiating the fixing, maintaining, changing or arranging of terms and conditions of employment regardless of whether or not the disputants stand in proximate relationship of employers and employees. 16. Regular Working Hours - the normal hours of work of any employee shall not exceed eight (B) hours a day. It shall include all time during which an employee is required to be on duty and/or to be at a prescribed workplace; all time during which an employee is permitted to work; and rest periods of short duration during working hours. (Labor Code Book III, Article 83 and recent jurisprudence) 17.Oveftime Pay - refers to the additional compensation for work peformed beyond eight (B) hours a day, which consists of an additional compensation equivalent to his regular wage plus at least 25olo thereof. Work performed beyond eight hours on a holiday or rest day shall be paid an additional compensation equivalent to the rate of the first eight hours plus at least 30o/o thereof. 18. Holiday Pay - refers to the payment of the regular daily wage for any unworked regular holiday. Ord. No. 0585-21 A. For Regular Holidays- the employee is entitled to at least 1000/o of his or her minimum wage rate even if he/she did not repoft to work, provided he/she is present or is on leave of absence with pay on the work day immediately preceding the holiday. Worked performed on that day merits at least twice (200olo) of the daily wage of the employee. As used in this provision, "holiday" includes: New Year's Day, Maundy Thursday, Good Friday, the ninth of April, the first of May, the twelfth of June, the fourth of July, the thiftieth of November, the twenty-fifth and thiftieth of December, and the day designated by law for holding a general election. B. For Special days - work performed on special days merits additional compensation of at least thirty (30o/o) of the basic wage or a total of one hundred thirly percent (130%). Where the employee works on a special day falling on his rest day, he/she shall be entitled to an additional compensation of at least fifty percent (50%) of his/her basic wage or a total of one hundred fifty percent (150o/o). Note that workers who are not required or permitted to work on special days are not entitled to any compensation. Unless otherwise modified by law, order, or proclamation, the following are the four (4) special days in a year under Executive Order No. 292, as amended by Republic Act 9849, as fufther amended by Republic Act No. 109661, that shall be obserued in the Philippines: Ninoy Aquino Day, Monday nearest August 21, All Saints Day November 1, Feast of the Immaculate Conception of Mary December B, Last Day of the Year December 31. 19.Seruice Incentive Leave - Every employee who has rendered at least one year of seruice shall be entitled to a yearly seruice incentive leave of five days with pay. 20. Minimum Wage Earner - this refers to salaried individuals earning a compensation of the daily minimum wage rates as determined by the Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board (RI/VPB).

text: OFFICE (WPDO) OF DAVAO CITY. - The Workers Protection and Development Office (WPDO) of Davao City shall be created under the Office of the City Mayor to protect the rights of the labor force and ensure the well-being of all workers within its jurisdiction and provide them with proper information of their rights and access to protection of their welfare. As such, a separate ordinance outlining the positions of the personnel under this office will be drafted to ensure the full function of the WPDO.

text: FUNCTIONS AND OBJECTIVES OF THE OFFICE. -The functions of the Davao City Workers Protection & Development Office (WPDO) are as follows: a. To initiate the organizing of Davao City Workers Council composed of: i. ii. iii. iv. 1 Representative from the Barangay; 1 Representative from Ununionized Sector; 1 Representative from Associations; 1 Representative from Labor Unions located in Davao City Ord. No. 0585-21 b. To superuise the Barangay Employment Service Desk (BESD) of the City and ensure its creation and submission of quarterly status repoft on employment seruices and reports within their respective jurisdiction; c. To produce educational and informational materials on the protection and promotion of basic rights of workers; Coordinate with DepEd, TESDA, Committee on Education for information campaign, City Mayor's Office, PESO, DOLE and NGOs Coordinate with Labor Unions to assist in the information dissemination d. To recommend sustainable livelihood programs for unemployed/displaced workers in coordination with DOLE, PESO and other government offices; e. To conduct research and provide trainings on the enforcement of general labor standards, occupational safety and health standards, social welfare laws and other pertinent laws affecting the welfare of the workers; f . To launch regular consultations with Davao City workers, employers, and labor organizations based on the principles of shared responsibility to promote understanding and industrial peace based on social justice; g. To conduct research on enforcement of labor standards (which includes pre-employment, human resources development, trainings, working conditions, implementation of proper wage rates, health, safety and social welfare benefits of workers), which shall include: Implementation of labor standards (statutory benefits like SSS, Philhealth, HDMF, and Social Security Benefits); Inspection of workplace by DOLE (by DOLE Inspectors, Inseft Visitorial Powers to do inspection of workplace and worker's condition through Labor Leaders and Management/Deputized Labor Inspectors); iii. Implementation of occupational safety for workers; Implementation of Safe Spaces Act, Sexual Harassment in the Workplace, Gender and Development Laws and Policies and new laws in the workplace; h. To enforce strict implementation of labor standards on employers and companies and monitor the same' i. To facilitate issues and concerns on labor relations (in coordination with various government agencies in charge of labor dispute, labor organizations, unions, unfair labor practices, CBAs and CNAs, strikes and lock outs and post employment) as defined by existing and relevant laws and statutes on labor and employment and coordinate with DOLE; j. To lead in the organizing of the City's activities for the annual commemoration of Labor Day every 1st day of May; i. i. ii iv ii Ord. No. 0585-21 k. To organize activities related to promotion of rights and welfare of women workers, solo parent's workers, qualified differently abled persons, abled workers with special needs and senior citizens and handicapped workers; l. To coordinate with existing local government offices engaged in Gender and Development (GAD), advocate and implement the same in all workplace; a. To establish an official Hotline or Social Media Accounts of WPDO and maintain an official contact number for BESD and publication of directory which includes PESO, DOLE, WPDO and Barangay BEDO, Labor Unions, Associations, Child Labor Focal Person, Task Force Against Child Labor, GAD, etc. m. To organize a network of volunteer lawyers and paralegal to assist and provide free legal seruices for workers, to wit: To assist in reaching an amicable settlement between the pafties involved; To prepare Drafting of Position Papers to be submitted to the NLRC; To provide free legal advice/assistance for and in behalf of workers;

TERM - The lease period for three (3) year commencing February 16, 2021 to February 15, 2024, based on the original terms and conditions as agreed upon by both parties. In the event that the LESSEE desires to renew this contract under this paragraph, the LESSOR shall be notified at least three (3) months before the expiration of the lease. 2. A five percent (5olo) per year escalation on the rental fees shall continue to be effective in any subsequent renewal of this Lease Contract. Without prejudice to the exercise by the LESSOR of its rights in Paragraph 12 and 17 herein, the LESSEE shall pay to the LESSOR interest at the rate of twenty four percentum (2r1olo) per annum on any monthly rental not paid, to be computed from the date of the delinquency. PAGE 2 - Contract of Lease 3. USES OF THE PREMISES - The LESSEE shall not use the leased premises for dwelling or sleeping purposes. The premises hereby leased shall be used o<clusively by the LESSEE for office and stockoom purposes and the latter shall not divert the premises to any other uses without the prior consent of the LESSOR, it being expressly agreed that if, at any time during the existence of this lease and without the previous consent of the LESSOR the said premises is used for any other purposes, the LESSOR reseryes the right or choice to, (a) rescind this contract in accordance with Paragraph L7, (b) increase the rental, or ( c) compel the LESSEE to stop the new activities. 4. IMPROVEMENT AND ALTERATIONS - The LESSEE shall not make any alterations, installations, additions or improvements of the leased premises, such as paftitions, shades, swings, blinds, window guards, etc., without the consent of the LESSOR. It is fufther agreed that all such alterations, installations, additions or improvemenb, except movable furniture and fixtures, placed at the expense of the LESSEE and removable without defacing or injuring the leased premises, shall, if so elected by the LESSOR, become its property and shall remain, and be surrendered with the premises as patt of thereof, upon termination of the lease, without compensation to the LESSEE. If the LESSOR does not elect to retain such alteration, installations, additions or improvements, the premises shall be surrendered to their original condition at the expense of the LESSEE. The LESSOR reserves the right to refuse any alteration, installation, addition or improvement requested by the LESSEE if in the LESSOR'S opinion, there is just cause to warrant such refusal. 5. POWER CONSUMPTION AND CHARGES FOR UTILITIES - All electrical consumption and charges, fees and costs for telephone, water, and other utilities used by the LESSEE in the leased premises, shall be for its account. The LESSEE may, at ib discretion, install a separate meter and convenience outlets and all electrical connections as it may deem necessary. 6. SIGNS AND ADVERTISEMENTS - To insure uniformity of design, the LESSEE shall not cause to be affixed, inscribed or painted, any notice, sign or other advertising medium, on any paft of the building without the consent of the LESSOR. The LESSEE shall not permit or give consent to any other person or entity to advetise, as if said person or entity uses, holds office, or is otherwise established, at the premises leased, or any part thereof, and unless the LESSOR agrees to the contrary, only the name and nomenclature of the LESSEE as written in the contract of lease shall be placed in the building directory and adveftised at or near the main door of the premises leased. No other sign or advertisement may be placed in the leased premises other than the place herein above indicated. Page 3 - Contract of Lease 7. CARE OF THE LEASED PREMISES - The LESSEE shall maintain the leased premises in a clean and sanitary condition, free from noxious odors and disturbing noise, and upon expiration of the lease, shall surrender and return the leased premises and fixtures in as good condition, except ordinary wear and tear, as the leased premises were actually found at the beginning of the lease. 8. RULES, REGUI-ATIONS, ETC. - The LESSEE will comply with any and all reasonable rules and safety regulations which may be promulgated from time to time by the LESSOR and made known to the LESSEE in writing, for the administration/use/occupancy of the leased premises, and with all the rules, regulations, ordinances and laws made by the health and duly constituted authorities of the City National Government, arising from or regarding the use, occupancy and sanitation of leased premises. The LESSEE shall indemnify and hold harmless the said LESSOR against all actions, suits, damages and claims by whosoever they may be brought or made by reason of the non-observance or non-performance of the said rules, regulations, ordinances, or laws, or of any covenants of this SECTION, without prejudice to the right of the LESSOR to cancel this lease in accordance with the penal provisions hereinafter contained. 9. INSPECTION OF PREMISES - The LESSOR or its authorized agent shall, by previous arrangement with the LESSEE, and after presenting his/her authority, have the right to enter the leased premises at any reasonable time, to examine the same, subject to security requirements of thc LESSEE, and during the last three (3) months of the term of the lease, to exhibit the leased premises to prospective tenants, except when this lease has been renewed as herein provided. 10. REPAIRS - The LESSEE shall make necessary repairs on the leased premises and maintain the same in good and tenantable condition. During the existence of this lease, the LESSEE shall pay for the cost of repairs, replacements, andlor restoration of damages caused on the leased premises by the herein LESSEE, its employees, representatives, agents, clients and/visitors. The LESSEE shall at all times, subject to prior arrangement, allow and extend access to the LESSOR to the leased premises for the purpose of making repairs, remodeling or repainting or to undertake all work necessary for the preservation, improvement or decoration of the building or any part thereof . No compensation or claims shall be allowed against the LESSOR by reason of inconvenience, annoyance or injury to the LESSEES business that may arise by viftue of undertaking any rarork under this provision. TERMINATION OF LEASE - Should the LESSEE opt not to renew the lease, LESSEE agrees to return and surrender to the LESSOR the leased premises at the end of the term of this lease in as good condition as reasonable wear and tear will permit and without delay whaboever, devoid of all occupants, furniture, afticles and effects of any kind other than such alterations, additions or improvement which shall be subject to the provisions of Paragraph 5. 12. SUB-LEASE, TRANSFER OR LEASE - The LESSEE shall not assign or transfer its right in this contract nor sub-lease or sublet all or any part of the leased premises, without the prior written consent of the LESSOR and no right title or interest thereto shall be conferred or vested in anyone other than the LESSEE without such written consent. 13. OCCUPATION OF THE LEASED PREMISES - After this lease has been terminated for any reason whatsoever, if the LESSEE continues the occupation of the leased premises with the consent of the LESSOR, said extension of lease shall be understood as running from month to month only, under the same terms and conditions herein stipulated and may be terminated by either party by means of a written notice served upon the other party at least 30 days prior to the date of such termination. 14. INFLAMMABLE AND DPLOSIVE MATERLALS - The LESSEE shall not bring into or store, nor shall allow third persons to bring into or store, in the leased premises anything of a highly inflammable nature or explosive materials, nor cook or install any apparatus, machinery or equipment which may expose the leased premises to fire or increase the fire hazard of the property or change the insurance rate of the property or any other article which the LESSOR may reasonably prohibit, it being understood that should the LESSEE do so, such violation may cause the LESSOR to order for the immediate removal of the abovementioned articles from the premises. 15. INSURANCE - The LESSOR shall insure the property up to the extent of its insurable interest and against all perils it may choose to be covered; the Lessee may also insure at its expense its propefi/improvement brought into the leased premises against perils it may want insured against. 16. NON - WAIVER - The failure of the LESSOR to insist upon a strict performance of any of the terms, conditions and covenants hereof shall not be deemed a relinquishment or waiver of any rights or remedy that said lessor may own/ nor shall it be construed as a waiver of any subsequent brcach or default of the terms, conditions and covenants hereof, which shall continue to be in full force and effect. No waiver by the LESSOR of any of its rights under this contract shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the LESSOR. Page 5 - Contract of Lease 17. PAYMENT OF REALTY TAXES - it shall be the duty of the LESSOR to pay the realty taxes on the land where the property is constructed as well as the property itself. 18. DAMAGE TO LEASED PREMISES - In case of damage to the leased premises or its appuftenance by fire, eafthquake, war or any others unforeseen cause, the LESSEE shall give immediate notice thereof to the LESSOR. If the lease premises shall be damaged by fire or other cause without the fault or negligence of the LESSEE or its agents, employees, servants, or visitors, the injury shall be repaired at the expense of the LESSOR within the reasonable time after such notice; however, if the building of the leased premises is deskoyed to such extent as to make it untenantable without the fault or neglect of the LESSEE, either party may demand the rescission of the contract. The LESSEE shall be fully liable to the LESSOR in all cases where damage of any nature or kind is caused by the fault or negligence of the said LESSEE, his employees, agents, seryants, or visitors. No compensation or claim shall be allowed against the LESSOR by reason of any inconvenience, annoyance or injury to the LESSEE'S business arising out of the necessity of repairing any poftion of the building, in whatever way such necessity may arise. 19. LOAD - No portion of the floor in said premises shall be loaded in excess of 32 kilos (70 lbs.) per square foot, nor shall any safe or other article weighing in excess of 200 kilos (44O lbs.) be placed in or removed from the premises without the knowledge and consent of the LESSOR, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. 20. INJURY oR DAMAGE TO THIRD PERSONS OR LEASE - The LESSEE hereby assume full responsibility for any and all damage which may be caused to persons or property while remaining either casually or in business in any part of the premises leased to the LESSEE and further binds himself to hold the LESSOR free and harmless from any such claims for injury or damage unless such injury or damage is due to the negligence of the LESSOR. The LESSOR shall neither be liable nor responsible for: a. the presence of bugs, vermin, ant anay, insects, if any, in the leased premisesl or b. for the failure of the water supply andlor electric; or for any adicle delivered or left to any of its employees, or c d. for any injury, loss or damage, which the LESSEE, his agents or employees may sustain in the premises due to any cause whatsoever, except when the cause of said injury, loss or damage is the negligence of the LESSOR; or Page 6 - Contract of Lease e. for damages occasioned by or arising from, plumbing, gas, water, and/or other pipes or air-conditioning system, or the bursting, Ieaking or destruction of any cistern, tan( water, closet, or water pipe in, above, upon said Jeased premises, nor for any damages arising from acts, nor negligence of the LESSEE or ib agents, employees, representatives, or any and all othcr persons. 21. EPROPRLATION - In the event that expropriation proceedings are instituted during the period of this lease by any instrumentality of the Government or by any other entity with authority to exercise such power, either party may rescind this contract should the leased premises become no longer useful for the purpose of this lease upon giving the other party thirty (30) days previous written notice thereof, In case of such expropriation, the LESSEE hereby unconditionally relieves and releases the LESSOR from any and all liability under this contract in connection with or arising out of such expropriation proceedings, without prejudice to whatever recourse the LESSEE may have against the expropriating entity on account of damage done or caused it to its propefties. 22. FAILURE TO SURRENDER - If said premises be not surrendered at the expiration of the term, the LESSEE shall pay, by way of penalty, a sum equivalent to the amount of the rentals for the leased premises for the whole period of delay. It is hereby agreed that such penalty shall likewise be without prejudice to the attorney's fees and other liabilities provided in this contract. The LESSEE shall furthermore hold the lessor harmless from any liability in respect to any and all claims made by any succeeding tenant against the LESSOR resulting from the delay by the LESSOR, in delivering possession of the premises to such succeeding tenant, insofar as such is occasioned by the failure of the LESSEE to surrender the premises on time. 23. DISTURBANCE - Disturbance or discontinuance of the possession of the leased premises by the LESSEE by causes beyond the control of the LESSOR shall confer no right of any kind to the LESSEE as against the LESSOR. 24. LEASE E(CLUDES PORTION OF BUILDING - This lease does not extend to the oubide portion of the building corresponding to or opposite the leased premises and the painting, gutting or affixing of business notices, signs or any other advertising medium in accordance with paragraph No. 5 of this contract shall not be construed as an extension of this lease to that portion outside of the building. 25. ABANDONMENT OF LEASE - In case the leased premises shall be deserted or vacated before the expiration of this lease, the LESSOR shall have the option to let the same as the agent of the LESSEE to receive the rent therefore and to apply the same for the payment of the rent due hereunder, holding the LESSEE for any deficiency . The venue of action shall be in Davao City to the exclusion of other courts . 28. RENTAL FOR REMAINING TERMS, SATISFACTION OR DAMAGES AND OBUGATION - In all cases where this contract is terminated or canceled, whether judicially of extra-judicially by reason of any default or breach committed by the LESSEE, the said LESSEE shall be fully liable to the LESSOR for the rentals corresponding to the remaining term of this lease, as well as for any and all damage actual or consequential, resulting from such default and termination, All remedies granted to the LESSOR under this contract or elsewhere shall be deemed cumulative. In case the LESSEE wants to vacate the leased premises before the expiration of this contract, LESSEE shall send a written notice to vacate to the LESSOR ninety (90) days before moving out, and the LESSOR retains the option to either accept or reject such notice to vacate. DUTERTE, hereinafter referred to as the "CITY'; and The DAVAO CITY WATER DISTRICT, a public water utility created under Presidential Decree No. 198, as amended, with principal office address at Km. 2.5 Mac Arthur Highway, Matina, Davao City, Philippines, duly represented by the Chairperson of the Board of Directors, EDUARDO A. BANGAYAN, hereinafter referred to as the ,,DCWD"; WITNESSETH: WHEREAS, the CITY is committed to protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them. It is an environmental concern of the City to have a sustainable management of waterways to meet and safeguard the recreational and life supporting capacity of water. It is committed to improving the water quality of the water resource within its territory and acknowledges that large amounts of contaminants or discharges come from untreated domestic sewage discharges and trade wastes, or industrial liquid wastes, thereby causing significant health risks to people near the river, and those in residential areas affected by floods; WHEREAS, under SECTION 20 of RA 9275 or otherwise known as the Philippines Clean Water Act imposes upon local government units to share the responsibility in the management and improvement of water utility within their territorial j urisd ictions; WHEREAS, under SECTION 17, RA 7160 mandates local government units (LGUs) to effectively provide basic services and facilities to their constituents, 6including drainage and sewerage; h-- I WHEREAS, as provided for in SECTION 2, Article I of Ordinance No. 036310, SERIES of 2013 otherwise known as the Septage and Sewerage Management Ordinance, it is a declared policy of Davao City to adopt and implement a comprehensive and integrated septage and sewerage management program, which shall among others, reduce, if not eliminate, the prevalence of waterborne and excreta-related diseases and pollution in bodies of water and encourage greater publ ic-private partnership; WHEREAS, majority of the homes in Davao City use septic tanks as a way of providing partialtreatment of septage and sludge. WHEREAS, the sludge is being disposed without proper treatment due to the non-existence of an appropriate treatment facility that caters to this need. Thus, the waste is being discharged directly to the drainage canals, creeks and other bodies of water that become polluted; WHEREAS, the DCWD aims to establish a proper Septage Management Program which will include the construction of Septage Treatment Plant (SpTP); WHEREAS, a Feasibility Study for the proposed Septage Management Program was conducted by DCWD; WHEREAS, the Feasibility Study through the establishment of a Septage Management Program aims to reduce the pollution attributed to untreated septage discharge to protect our water resource, to improve water quality, sanitation and public health conditions, and provide efficient and affordable septage desludging service initially to existing DCWD customers and to alltargeted areas of DCWD; WHEREAS, the CITY enacted Ordinance No.0363-10 and Implementing Rules and Regulations prescribing the procedures in the establishment of Septage and Sewerage Management Program; and WHEREAS, the CITY has manifested its intent to support in the establishment of SpTP. ) NOW THEREFORE, the parties have agreed as follows: WHEREAS, SECTION 5 of Title II of the PD 198 provides for the formation of water districts to operate water supply and distribution systems, wastewater collection, treatment and disposal facilities and to conduct other functions and operations incidental to water resource development, utilization and disposal; I. PURPOSE The Parties seek to enter into MOA for the establishment, operation, maintenance and management of SpTP specifically mentioned in SECTION 22, Rule IX, IRR of City Ordinance No. 0363-10. IL OUTPUT To ensure commitment for the establishment, operation, maintenance and management of SpTP. III. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILTTIES A. The CITY shall: l. Grant DCWD the authority to construct SpTP; 2. Grant DCWD the authority to operate and maintain the SpTP in accordance with DOH standards; 3. Support and assist DCWD in the implementation of Septage Management Program; 4. Grant DCWD the authority to desludge all residential and commercial establishment within he territorial jurisdiction; 5. Ensure administration and enforcement of the Septage and Sewerage Ordinance and its Implementing Rules and Regulations; 6. Conduct a survey of all properties and premises in the CITY in coordination with the barangay officials to determine if a septic tank is present, and if it is accessible for desludging; 7 . Serve notices of non-conformance to the owners/administrators, or occupants in case of non-conforrnance with the provisions of the IRR; 8. Issue certificate of compliance to the property owners who are deemed to have met the minimum specifications for septic tanks as stated in the 'lL9. Keep a record of all owners/administrators of building and structures who have desludged their septic tanks, those that are inaccessible, those that do not have septic tanks, and those that do not have water-sealed toilets, and other data that may deemed necessary for the purpose of this MOA; 10. Conduct a periodic survey of properties every five (5) years to veriff changes in septic tank accessibility or changes in tank capacity requirements. This shall be done in coordination with the barangay officials; I l. Assist DCWD in facilitating and acquiring permits, clearances and documents required and related to the construction and establishment of the SpTP; 12. Make the necessary adjustment/update in the zonal classification of the area where the SpTP is to be constructed, when necessary, upon proper public consultation and favorable recommendation and approval of the SANGGUNIANG Panlungsod; and 13. The issuance of such authority above-enumerated is non-exclusive to DCWD and the City may enter into agreement with other entities for the implementation of a Septage and Sewerage Management Program in the City. The DCWD shall: Construct a SpTP. Fully bear the entire costs in the construction of the SpTP. Shoulder the operations and maintenance cost of the SpTP. 4. Impose the Septage Management Fee (SMF) and its mode of payment being subject further to the conditions as follows: a. For DCWD customers, SMF shall be added up to their monthly water bill which is computed as a uniform price per cubic meter of water consumed; b. The total monthly basic rate for the first l0 cubic meters of water consumption with the added SMF shall not exceed 5% of the average monthly income of the low-i ncome-group families in DCWD's franchise area; and B l. 2. J, c. For non-DCWD customers, the septage collection and treatment shall be handled by DCWD and shall be done on a per job order basis. Households shall pay SMF to DCWD on a"pay-per-service" scheme. 5. Impose the Treatment Fee as payment of the accredited private desludging service providers who would avail the septage treatment services of DCWD, based on a price per cubic meter of septage for treatment, a "pay-perseryice" scheme. 6. Pay the Desludging Fee to the City as per SECTION 40, Rule XIII, IRR of the City Ordinance No. 0363-10, or as may be adjusted by the City. 7. Determine the SMF for DCWD customers, and the Treatment Fee for private desludging service providers subject to the review and approval of the Local Water Utilities Administration. 8. Reserve the right to adjust the SMF rate and Treatment Fee for reasons such as: a. Increase in the capacity of the Septage Treatment Plant or the implementation of the subsequent phases of the plant. b. Any other circumstances that may warrant improvement and expansion ofthe SpTP and such other services. C. BOTH PARTIES shall: 1. Support the operation and management of the Septage Management Program 2. Extend mutual cooperation to each other to ensure smooth implementation of the Septage Management Program; 3. Exchange information and / or views with each other with respect to any matters necessary for successful completion of environmental impact study of the project; 4. to all Parties; Consult each other at any time on any matters of common interest 5. Deliberate on any matter in an appropriate period in order to facilitate the coordination among concerned agencies and accomplish the objectives of this MOA; and 6. lnstitute and spearhead the advocacy and promotional activities for the dissemination of the information, education and communication campaign for the Septage Management Program. ry. BINDING AND TERMINATION The Parties are entering into this MOA while wishing to maintain their own separate and unique missions and mandates, and their own accountabilities. Unless specifically provided otherwise, the cooperation between the Parties as outlined in this MOA is not to be considered or construed as a partnership or other type of legal entity or personality. Nothing in this MOA shall be construed as superseding or interfering in any way with other agreements or contracts entered into between the Parties, either prior to or subsequent to the signing of MOA. This MOA shall be for a period of fifty (50) years commencing from the date of notarization, renewable Ibr another twenty-five (25) years by giving written notice to renew at least ninety (90) days prior to the expiration of the original fiftyyear term, upon terms and conditions mutually agreed by the parties. Any party may terminate this MOA only for valid and just cause. text: DEFINITION OF TERMS.- ARBOR DAY refers to a one-day activity of tree planting and other forms of relevant activities held annually. GREENING PLAN refers to the City's contribution to the National Greening Program whereby specific activities relative, but not limited to, seedling production and tree planting are conducted. PLANTING OF TREE refers to the planting of perennial plant, either fruit bearing tree or forest tree that grows to a height of several feet including mangrove. MAINTENANCE OF TREE refers to nufturing of the seedlings after the planting until they are stabilized in the field.

text: DECLARATI9N OF DAVAO CITY ARBOF. DAY. The celebration of Arbor Day in the City of Davao shall be on the 25th day of June of every year. The City Mayor is hereby granted authority to issue the necessary proclamations in accordance with SECTION 4 of Republic Act No. 10176. The City, however, may allow a separate day for the actual date of tree planting, whenever necessary, considering the suitable planting season, unpredictable changes of the weather, and availability of pafticipants.

text: GENERAL PROVISIONS. a. The City Government of Davao, all its departments and offices, together with all the Barangays of the City, shall initiate tree planting activities every year in celebration of the Arbor Day of the City of Davao. The City Environment and Natural Resources Office and the City Agriculturist's Office, in coordination with the Department of Environment and Natural Resources, may identify the areas for the Tree Planting Activity and the trees to be planted. b. The foregoing notwithstanding, all able-bodied officials and employees of the City Government of Davao are required to plant and nufture one (1) tree every year as paft of their duty and responsibility, whether it be planted in a common public tree planting site or in a private estate. c. All employees of National Government Agencies with office in the City of Davao, Non-Government Organizations (NGOs) and People's Organizations, public and private schools, universities, private offices and enterprises and other business establishments operating in the City of Davao may set a different day within the year to celebrate Arbor Day to conduct tree planting activities whether it be in a common public tree planting site or in a private estate. All able-bodied employees of National Government Agencies with office in the City of Davao and able-bodied individuals from Non-Government Organizations (NGOs) and People's Organizations, public and private schools, universities, private offices and enterprises and other business establishments operating in the City of Davao, who are at least twelve (12) years of age, are encouraged to plant and support at least one (1) tree every year. a Ord. For purposes of this Ordinance, the planting of bamboo shall be considered as compliance to the provisions hereof and the planting thereof is encouraged along riverbanks. e. Tree planting activity shall be done preferably in: a) Public lands, forestparks, and watershed areas; b) Public parks in urban and rural areas; c) Riverbanks (preferably for bamboo); d) Public school grounds, gardens or other available areas within the school premises; e) Private schools, parks and lands with the consent of the owner thereof; D Protection Water Use Sub-Zone; Mangrove Sub-Zone; Rivers, Creeks and Lakes Sub-Zone; Wetlands Sub-Zone; Marine Protected Area Sub-Zone; Production Water Sub-Zone; Aquaculture Sub-Zone; Municipal Fishing SubZone, for Mangrove tree planting. In case the violator opts to voluntarily render community seruice, he/she shall secure from the Office of the City Mayor or the City ENRO, as may be authorized by the City Mayor, an assigned environmental protection related community seruice that will be required of the violator, including, but not limited, to clean-up activity, greening and tree planting activity, solid waste management activity, wastewater management activity, or Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) seruice. text: DECLARATION OF POLICIES - Davao City recognizes the vital role of the youth in nation-building enshrined in the 1987 Philippine Constitution. It shall promote and protect their physical, moral, spiritual, intellectual and social well-being. Thus, it shall be the policy of Davao City to defend the rights of the children and provide special protection from all forms of sexual abuse that are prejudicial to their development. Speciflcally, the City shall provide comprehensive measures and strategies in combating the proliferation of sexual abuse against children by engaging and harmonizing the effofts of governmental and non-governmental agencies. The City shall continue its tireless effort in giving priority to the rights of the children especially in terms of protection which led the City in consistently winning awards as one of the best child-friendly cities in the country, among others.
