text: DEFINITION OF TERMS. 1. Center-based programs - refer to the programs in an establishment where people can seek to avail strategic programs, seruices and interventions developed for purposes of protecting children against sexual abuse. 2. Child (Children) - for purposes of this Ordinance, child (children) refers to person(s) below eighteen (18) years of age or those over but unable to fully take care of themselves and protect themselves from sexual abuse because of physical and/or mental disability condition. (CWC 20L9, with minor edits) 3. Child (Children) at high-risk against rape - refers to a child who is exposed to a higher level of danger against sexual abuse compared to other children due to risk factors and conditions affecting him or her. 4. Child Pornography the unlawful or prohibited acts defined and punishable by Republic Act No. 9775 or the Anti-Child Pornography Act of 2009, committed through a computer system: Provided, That the penalty to be imposed shall be one (1) degree higher than that provided for in Republic Act No. 9775. 5. Community-based programs - refer to the programs provided by persons, offices or organizations through approaching the community with strategic programs, seruices and interyentions developed for purposes of protecting children against sexual abuse. 6. Consciousness building - an approach to a child in awakening and/or improving his or her state of mind specifically in realizing the evil sought by sexual abuse and his or her vulnerability to it. 7. Cybersex against a child - the willful engagement, maintenance, control, or operation directly or indirectly, of any lascivious exhibition of sexual organs or sexual activity, with the aid of a computer system, for favor or consideration against a child. Ord. No. 0854-22 B. Empowerment - an approach to a child in making him or her stronger and more confident specifically in protecting his or her right against sexual abuse. 9. Responsible agencies -these are the agencies that are mentioned and given specific roles in this Ordinance. 10. Sexual abuse on child - refers to an act in which a child is abused for sexual gratification. It includes direct sexual contact, engagement in indecent exposure (of the genitals, nipples, etc.), pornography, prostitution and other forms of sexual gratification involving a child.

text: COMMITTEE ON CHILDREN PROTECTION AGAINST SEXUAL ABUSE. A Committee is hereby created to address the issue on sexual abuse against children. It shall be composed of the following: Chairperson - Special Office for Children's Concern (SOCC) Vice-Chairperson - City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO) Secretariat - Integrated Gender and Development Division (IGDD) Members: 1. Representative of Local Council for the Protection of Children (LCPC) 2. Representative of the Barangay Council for the Protection of Children (BCPC) 3. Representative from the Sanggunian Kabataan (SK) Federation 4. Representative from Davao City Police Office (DCPO) 5. Representative from City Information Office (CIO) 6. Representative from City Health Office (CHO) 7. Representative from the Division Office of the Depaftment of Education (DepEd), through its Division Office B. Representative from the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCrP) RO xr 9. Representative from the National Commission of Muslim Filipinos (NCMF) RO XI 10. Representative from the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) RO XI ll.Representative from Local Media Board 12. Representative from Local Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) working on Children's Rights 13. Representative from private schools The Committee shall have the following duties and functions: 1. Overall function. It shall lead in attaining the objective of this Ordinance pafticularly in building the capacity of the local community in giving protection to children against sexual abuse by harmonizing the roles and efforts of the responsible agencies herein established. 2. Implementation oversight and monitoring. It shall be responsible to oversee and monitor the implementation of this Ordinance. 3. Meetings. It shall convene regularly to discuss any matters relevant to the issue, formulate policies, objectives, guidelines and/or other matters to have an efficient and effective implementation of this Ordinance. Ord. No. 0854-22 4. Inter-agency coordination and linkages. The SOCC and CSWDO, being the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson respectively, shall ensure the proper coordination and linkages of the responsible agencies in executing their roles provided herein. 5. Data Modernization. It shall relevant information submitted to them by the responsible agencies gathered in the course of executing their roles. The data shall be used to conduct situation analysis in order to formulate supplemental measures and strategies to fufther enhance and strengthen protection of children against sexual abuse. A systematic approach shall be established. Thus, the following mechanisms may be considered. a) Establish a Profiling System from the information submitted to them by the responsible agencies. b) Establish and maintain a master list and database of children all-over the city. The SOCC shall coordinate with the barangays and concerned agencies for the regular submission of relevant child-related information. These records peftaining to the information given to them shall be confidential and shall only be disclosed to proper authorities. c) Utilize the data gathered and provide a Situation Assessment and Analysis on Children relative to protection of children against sexual abuse. It shall also determine who are the children considered at a high-risk of being sexually abused and provide recommendations and action plans thereof to the Committee. The Situation Analysis can be used to identiff who are the children considered at a high-risk of being sexually abused and determine the risk factors and conditions that contribute to the incident such as: i. Risky behaviors of the perpetrator; ii. Handicapped victims or children with disabilities; iii. Povety-stricken families; iv. Out-of-school youth; v. Dysfunctional households and abusive parents; vi. Those who live in isolated and/or far-flung remote communities' and vii. Other risk factors and conditions. d) As an end-product, provide a Local State of Children Repoft policy proposals and guidelines on how to address the situation and provide better protection for children against all forms of sexual abuse. e) The report shall be submitted to the Office of the City Mayor for any purpose it may deem proper. 6. Ensuring the functionality of programs and interuentions. It shall conduct periodic assessment regarding the programs and interuentions provided by responsible agencies. Identify the gaps existing therein and determine which programs and interuentions are non-functioning or has overlapping functions and those which are ineffective, inefflcient and needs reconsideration, and provide remedies thereto. Ord. No. 0854-22 It must ensure that these programs and interuentions are age-appropriate, gender-sensitive and culturally-appropriate. It shall always provide utmost consideration to the best interest of the child. 7. Initiating Partnership with other agencies. It shall have the initiative to tap additional workforce and advocates for children protection such as Nongovernment Organizations (NGOs), Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), Faithbased Organizations and other volunteers and invite them to have joint effofts in combating sexual abuse on children, B. Other functions. Perform such other functions necessary to achieve the objectives of this Ordinance. ROLE OF Crry TNFORMATTON OFFTCE (CrO)

text: SCHOOL-BASED PROGRAMS. The Department of Education (DepEd), through its Division Office and in coordination with the Child Protection Committee (CPC) created within the school, shall aid in strengthening children protection against sexual abuse through the following measures and strategies: 1. Conduct various advocacies, campaigns and other forms of information dissemination activities for purposes of raising awareness on children protection against sexual abuse in a school-setting. The Division Office may coordinate with the City Information Office for purposes of implementing this provision. 2. Formulate and implement child protection policies, guidelines and procedures for quick response and appropriate referral system for purposes of enhancing and strengthening child protection and safety against sexual abuse in a school-setting. 3. In coordination with CSWDO and SOCC, conduct training for teachers and other school personnel relating to protection of children against sexual abuse in a school-setting such as: a. Equipping them with the ability to recognize potential indicators of sexual abuse incidents among the students; b. Equipping them with the ability to influence children in mentally conditioning them on how to protect themselves from the vices of sexual abuse and their vulnerability to it. They shall aid in building resiliency, self-esteem and psychological competence of students against sexual abuse through providing them appropriate information knowledge and skills; c. Conduct training in handling incidents of sexual abuse committed to students specifically on repofting to appropriate agencies including referral to rehabilitation centers, providing comfort to victims and maintaining the confidentiality thereof; d. Ensure that they are well-oriented with laws relating to sexual abuse, including this Ordinance, and determine their duties and the rights of the students embodied therein; e. Members of the Committee on Decorum and Investigation (CODI) and other officers created pursuant to Safe Spaces City Ordinance of Davao City shall participate in the training and be equipped with competence to handle cases of sexual abuse involving children; PageT of 15 Ord. No. 0854-22 4. Develop and incorporate in the curriculum of the children in public or private schools with information that will enable them to understand the vices of sexual abuse and their vulnerability to it and mentally condition in them the necessity to protect themselves from it. Also, develop age-appropriate, gender-sensitive and cultural-appropriate information materials relating to protection of children against sexual abuse. The DepEd, in coordination with IGDD and CSWDO, shall provide Child Protection Policy Modules to fufther strengthen the city's child protection program and empower children to seek protection against abusers. Encourage the students to provide anti-sexual abuse activities to be included in the plans of the student government/councils, clubs or organizations, cocurricular activities and other school-based programs; 5. Establish a Master list and Database on Students where records pertaining to the information of students shall be kept confldentially; 6. Provide a Situation Assessment and Analysis to determine who are those students that are considered at high-risk of being sexually abused. The Situation Analysis can be used to determine the school-based risk factors and conditions that contribute to incidents of sexual abuse on children. It shall also give recommendations to the Committee necessary to enhance and strengthen the protection of children against sexual abuse. 7. Ensure that hotlines and other venues for repofting incidents of sexual abuse are posted in the conspicuous premises of the school. B. It shall serue as repository of information related to sexual abuse in schoolsetting and shall maintain reports of incidents and cases of all schools. The records shall be confidential and only upon the request of proper agencies such as the Committee, coufts, police and others that the same shall be disclosed. 9. Provide for other mechanisms that will further enhance and strengthen protection of children against sexual abuse and develop a safe and protective environment. The provisions laid down in DepEd Order No. 40, SERIES of 2012, shall apply herein suppletorily. ROLE OF CITY SOCIAL WELFARE AND DEVELOPMENT OFFICE (CSWDO)

text: LIFE-SKILL TRAININGS. The CSWDO shall also conduct life-skill trainings to the members of the family. a) Children should be able to learn life-skills against all forms of sexual abuse such as, but not limited to, the following: Recognition skills - A child should be able to determine sexual invitations and innuendos of the perpetrator. He or she should also be able to identify risk indicators such as when he or she is isolated with a stranger. Further, he or she should become more cautious and vigilant in the place and people around him or her. ii. Communication skills - Knowing how to refuse sexual invitations and innuendos of the perpetrator. Practical and feasible self-defense skills - it may tap the DCPO or other agencies with competency to provide such skills. Reporting skills - A child should be guided where to repoft incidents and seek aid. These may include parents, relatives, teachers, barangay officials, police officers, and hotlines. That if he or she is threatened, the child should be able to know how he/she can seek assistance and whom he or she can approach. b) Parents and other persons with parental authority shall be equipped with skills appropriate for protecting the child from any forms of sexual abuse such as, but not limited to, the following: i. iii iv Ord. text: ROLE OF DCPO. The Davao City Police Office (DCPO) shall have the following duties and responsibilities: 1. text: RATIONALE AND CONSIDERATIONS FOR ESTABLISHING A LOCALIZED CICC. The rationale and considerations for establishing a localized CICC are as follows: 1. The creation of CICC of Davao City as well as its composition and functions was inspired from the creation of Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) under Republic Act No. 10175 or the 'tCybercrime Prevention Act of 2012". Hence, the functions and responsibilities are already existing as well as the tools, machineries and expeftise of personnel. 2. In this proposed Ordinance, it aims to localize the functions of CICC under RA 10175 and took consideration of the following criteria: Ord. No. 0854-22 a. The provisions were tailored to address online sexual abuse on children; b. In contrast with the National CICC, the localized version of CICC will tend to put more focus on addressing the sexual abuse on children within the city taking into consideration the specific attributable factors and conditions existing within the city. c. It will hopefully magnify the efforts in combating sexual abuse against children since the efforts to be rendered are more isolated and focused in the city compared to the general overview of national CICC. d. The specific local agencies involved are hereby determined. e. The coordination and linkages among the local CICC to the national and international on intelligence, investigations, training and capacity building are hereby established; f. text: MEDIA HANDLING OF NEWS AND ISSUES INVOLVING CHILDREN.- Pursuant to Republic Act No. 9344, the mass media shall play an active role in the promotion of child rights, and delinquency prevention by relaying consistent messages through a balanced approach. Media practitioners shall, therefore, have the duty to maintain the highest critical and professional standards in repofting and covering cases of children in conflict with the law. In all publicity concerning children, the best interest of the child should be the primordial and paramount concern. text: DECLARATION OF PRINCIPLES AND POLICIES A. The City Government of Davao is committed to the maintenance of peace and security within its jurisdiction, as a safe and peaceful environment is vital to the progress of a city when there are no risks and threats to its development. B. Implementing and policymaking bodies are created for the purpose of peacebuilding. C. Therc are eight (8) broad categories that create and sustain peaceful societies. The Institute for Economics and Peace has identified the following eight (8) Pillars of PosiUve Peace as the most common characteristics of most peaceful societies. These pillars are: . Well-functioning government; o Low levels of corruption; . Acceptance of the rights of others; . Good relations with neighbors; . Sound business environment; o High level of human capital; . Equitable distribution of resources; and o Free flow of information. The concept of Positive Peace acknowledges that ending direct violence alone does not guarantee durable peace. Ending direct violence is Negative Peace. For peace to endure, a society must build longer-term conditions that enable society to unify and flourish. This is called Positive Peace. Investing in Positive Peace improves resilience, mitigates risks of violence, and reduces the economic toll from conflict. The Eight-Pillars of Positive Peace are highly interconnected and interact together to build a system. It therefore requires building capacities for peace, not only of the government, but also of local communities and other structures and institutions of the city. The establishment of Peace 911- The Center For Peacebuilding will contribute to the achievement of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals of the United Nations, in particular, Goal 16 on building peace, justice and strong institutions, strengthening human rights, reducing discrimination and inequality, promoting gender equality, preseruing natural resources and protecting the climate. D. Republic Act TLGI SECTION 3(b) states that there shall be established in every local government unit an accountable, efficient, and dynamic organizational structure and operating mechanism that will meet the priority needs and seruice requirements of its communities; and 3 (h) there shall be a continuing mechanism to enhance local autonomy not only by legislative enabling acts but also by administrative and organizational reforms. Ord. No. 0891-22 E. Republic Act 7160, SECTION 76 states that every local government unit shall design and implement its own organizational structure and staffing pattern taking into consideration its service requirements and financial capacity, subject to the minimum standards and guidelines prescribed by the Civil Service Commission. F. Republic of the Philippines Executive Order No. 70, SERIES of 2018, Institutionalizing the Whole-Of-Nation Approach in Attaining Inclusive and Sustainable Peace, Creating a National Task Force to end Local Communist Armed Conflict, and Directing the Adoption of A National Peace Framework". G. title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING THE MAINTENANCE OF IDLE POLES AND ABANDONED WIRES AND CABLES IN THE CITY OF DAVAO

text: DECLARATION OF POLICY - Along some streets of Davao City are untidily scattered with idle poles, strewn with abandoned and unused wires, cables and unbundled or nonfunctional overhead electrical wires and communication cables that not only present unpleasant sight and view but also posing hazard to persons and propefties. This Ordinance aims to regulate the maintenance of abandoned wires, cables and poles considered as nuisance within the City. This will create a safe and clean environment for individuals protecting them from harm or injury that may be caused by abandoned wires, cables and poles. Ord. No. 0B9B-22
title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING THE MAINTENANCE OF IDLE POLES AND ABANDONED WIRES AND CABLES IN THE CITY OF DAVAO

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - For purposes of this Ordinance, the following terms are defined: 3.1 Abandoned wires - refer to wires and cables installed and seruing no purpose; 3.2 Barangay Inventory-refers to the inventory submitted by the barangay consisting of a list of all abandoned wires, cables and idle poles within their jurisdiction, with actual pictures of the color-coded wires, pole number and exact location; 3.3 Cable- an assembly of one or more insulated conductors or optical fibers within an enveloping sheath that supply electricity or telecommunications signals; 3,4 Color-coded wires - refer to wires and cables marked with ceftain colors that identify the ownership of such wires; 3.5 Idle poles - refer to all poles installed which are no longer in use or dilapidated; 3.6 Incident Report - refers to the report issued by the Wires and Cables Technical Team after a priority-tagging of the Barangay inventory; 3.7 Nuisance - refers to any act, omission, establishment, business, condition of property, or anything else which injures or endangers the health or safety of others; 3.8 Overhead Lines - all kinds of wires and cables installed overhead; 3.9 Pole - refers to utility poles or columns used to support attachments for all kinds of overhead lines, cables and accessories.
title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING THE MAINTENANCE OF IDLE POLES AND ABANDONED WIRES AND CABLES IN THE CITY OF DAVAO

text: GUIDELINES AND REGULATED ACTS - The following acts shall be obserued in the implementation of this Ordinance: 4,1 Removal of Abandoned Wires and Idle Poles - Abandoned wires and idle poles that are considered as nuisance must be removed within thity (30) days from receipt of a written notice. Any wire or cable that is not removed on the 3'd offense shall be removed by the Ancillary Seruices Unit subject to the permission of the Wires and Cables Technical Team. 4.2 Bundling of Wires and Cables - Loose, unbundled or cluttered wires, and cables that are still in seruice shall be bundled or bound together to form a single unit by the use of zip tie, tie wire or by lashing, or by the use of any other strong and safe material. An Incident Repoft must be filed with the Wires and Cables Technical Team. Violations under this Ordinance must be treated per Incident Repoft. Failure to obserue the abovementioned acts shall be a violation of this Ordinance and shall be penalized accordingly. For this purpose, the barangay shall be informed prior to any installation of wires and cables within their jurisdiction.

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS (a) Ambulant, Transient or Itinerant Vendor - refers to a vendor or seller who does not permanently occupy a definite place of the market but one who comes either daily or occasionally to sell his/her goods. (b) Account Opening Day or Account On-Boarding Day - is an activity wherein QR Ph-participating Financial Service Providers (FSPs), together with personnel from Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), will assist covered userc and their clients in opening an account, including the provision of QR Code printouts that can be readily displayed in their stores, terminals, and vehicles. The LGU will detennine the designated days and places in the City (e.9., public markets, terminals, barangay halls) to conduct on-boarding activities. (c) Basic Deposit Account (BDA) - refers to interest or non-interest bearing bank account with an initial minimum deposit of no more than One Hundred Pesos (PhP100.00), no minimum maintaining balance, no dormancy charges, maximum balance of Fifty Thousand Pesos (PhP50,000.00) and with simplified know-your<ustomer or KYC requirements. The list of banks authorized by BSP to offer BDA can be found on the BSP website : https : //bit. lylBa nkswithBDAs. (d) Buyer - shall refer to a person who purchases goods, commodities or foodstuffs from a vendor or seller. (e) City Public Market - refers to a public market maintained, owned and/or operated by the City Government within its territorialjurisdiction. (0 Digital payment - refers to a monetary payment transaction between two (2) pafties through a digital payment instrument in which both the payer and the payee use an electronic channel. (g) Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT) - refers to transfer of funds between two (2) transaction accounts in the same or in different financial institutions superuised by the BSP, which are initiated and received using electonic devices and channels to transmit payment transactions. No. 0101-22 (h) Electronic Money (E-money) - a monetary value as represented by a claim on its issuer, that is: a. electronically stored in an instrument or device; b. issued against receipt of funds of an amount not lesser in value than the monetary value issued; c. accepted as a means of payment by persons or entities other than the issuer; d. withdrawable in cash or cash equivalent; e. issued in accordance with SECTION 702 of the BSP's Manual of Regulations for Banks. The list of e-money issuers (EMI) or entities authorized by BSP to offer e-money account can be found on the BSP website: https://bit.lylBSPSupervisedEMls. (i) Financial Seruice Providerc (FSP) - means a regulated financial institution which is licensed and superuised by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. The term refers to deposit-taking institutions, non-bank financial institutions and the mobile financial seruice providers. 0) Government-owned and/or Operated Public Markets - refer to those established out of public funds or those leased/acquired by any legal modes or means from private persons, natural or juridical, to be operated by the government either through its instrumentality, branch or political subdivisions. (k) InstaPay - an electronic fund transfer facility offered by a participating bank or EMI to its clients to allow them to instantly transfer funds from their account to another held in other pafticipating banks or EMI in the Philippines. The list of institutions participating in InstaPay can be found on the BSP website: https://bit.lyllnstapayQRPH. (l) Market Rental Fee - refers to the fee paid to and collected by the City Treasurer for the privilege of using public market facilities. (m) Motor vehicle - any conveyance designed to be self-propelled by engine, and includes any vehicles designed to be propelled by electric power obtained from overhear wires but not operated upon rails. (n) Peddler -any person, who either for himself or on commission, travels from place to place and sells his goods or offers to sell and deliver the same. Whether a peddler is a wholesale peddler or a retail peddler of a particular commodity shall be determined from the definitions of wholesale dealer or retail dealer as provided in the Revenue Code of the (o) Peddler, Hawker or Hustler - includes any person, whether adult or minor, who peddles or hawks goods, wares, merchandise, or any afticles, in any manner, from place to place; or one who offers for sale, afticles without any regular fixed and established place of business in Davao City. (p) Public Market -refers to any place, building or structure of any kind recognized as such under existing laws or ordinances and those to be established upon recommendation of the local government concerned. It embraces all market stalls, tiendas, buildings, roads, subways, waterways drainage and other connections, parking spaces, and other appuftenances thereto. (q) Public Market Vendor - any person, who, upon approval of this Ordinance, has been occupying one or more stalls in any public market, including privately owned but city-operated market with or without lease contract with the City of Davao. (s) QR Code - shoft for "Quick Response Code," a QR Code is a two-dimensional image-based bar code capable of holding large amounts of infonnation. QR Codes store information using patterns of black dots and white spaces, ananged in a square grid. It can be read by a smaftphone r:rmera that is equipped with a bar-code reader. When personal and financial information are stored in it, a QR Code can be used to send and receive money such as payment Uansactions. text: DECLARATION OF POLICIES - Davao City recognizes the vital role of the youth in nation-building enshrined in the 1987 Philippine Constitution. It shall promote and protect their physical, moral, spiritual, intellectual and social well-being. Thus, it shall be the policy of Davao City to defend the rights of the children and provide special protection from all forms of sexual abuse that are prejudicial to their development. Specifically, the City shall provide comprehensive measures and strategies in combating the proliferation of sexual abuse against children by engaging and harmonizing the efforts of governmental and non-governmental agencies. The City shall continue its tireless effort in giving priority to the rights of the children especially in terms of protection which led the City in consistently winning awards as one of the best child-friendly cities in the country, among others.

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS. 1. Center-based programs - refer to the programs in an establishment where people can seek to avail strategic programs, seruices and interuentions developed for purposes of protecting children against sexual abuse. 2. Child (Children) - for purposes of this Ordinance, child (children) refers to person(s) below eighteen (18) years of age or those over but unable to fully take care of themselves and protect themselves from sexual abuse because of physical and/or mental disability condition. (CWC 2019, with minor edits) 3. Child (Children) at high-risk against rape - refers to a child who is exposed to a higher level of danger against sexual abuse compared to other children due to risk factors and conditions affecting him or her. 4. Child Pornography - the unlawful or prohibited acts defined and punishable by Republic Act No. 9775 or the Anti-Child Pornography Act of 2009, committed through a computer system: Provided, That the penalty to be imposed shall be one (1) degree higher than that provided for in Republic Act No. 9775. 5. Community-based programs - refer to the programs provided by persons, offices or organizations through approaching the communi$l with strategic programs, seruices and interuentions developed for purposes of protecting children against sexual abuse. 6. Consciousness building - an approach to a child in awakening and/or improving his or her state of mindspecifically in realizing the evil sought by sexual abuse and his or her vulnerability to it. 7. Cybersex against a child - the willful engagement, maintenance, control, or operation directly or indirectly, of any lascivious exhibition of sexual organs or sexual activity, with the aid of a computer system, for favor or consideration against a child. t Ord. No. 0854-22 B. Empowerment - an approach to a child in making him or her stronger and more confident specifically in protecting his or her right against sexual abuse. 9. Responsible agencies -these are the agencies that are mentioned and given specific roles in this Ordinance. 10. Sexual abuse on child - refers to an act in which a child is abused for sexual gratification. It includes direct sexual contact, engagement in indecent exposure (of the genitals, nipples, etc.), pornography, prostitution and other forms of sexual gratification involving a child.

text: COMMITTEE ON CHILDREN PROTECTION AGAINST SEXUAL ABUSE. A Committee is hereby created to address the issue on sexual abuse against children. It shall be composed of the following: Chairperson - Special Office for Children's Concern (SOCC) Vice-Chairperson - City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO) Secretariat - Integrated Gender and Development Division (IGDD) Members: 1. Representative of Local Council for the Protection of Children (LCPC) 2. Representative of the Barangay Council for the Protection of Children (BCPC) 3. Representative from the Sanggunian Kabataan (SK) Federation 4. Representative from Davao City Police Office (DCPO) 5. Representative from City Information Office (CIO) 6. Representative from City Health Office (CHO) 7. Representative from the Division Office of the Depaftment of Education (DepEd), through its Division Office B. Representative from the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCrP) RO Xr 9. Representative from the National Commission of Muslim Filipinos (NCMF) RO XI 10. Representative from the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) RO XI ll.Representative from Local Media Board 12. Representative from Local Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) working on Children's Rights 13. Representative from private schools The Committee shall have the following duties and functions: 1. Overall function. It shall lead in attaining the objective of this Ordinance pafticularly in building the capacity of the local community in giving protection to children against sexual abuse by harmonizing the roles and effofts of the responsible agencies herein established. 2. Implementation oversight and monitoring. It shall be responsible to oversee and monitor the implementation of this Ordinance. 3. Meetings. It shall convene regularly to discuss any matters relevant to the issue, formulate policies, objectives, guidelines and/or other matters to have an efficient and effective implementation of this Ordinance. Ord. No. 0854-22 4. Inter-agency coordination and linkages. The SOCC and CSWDO, being the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson respectively, shall ensure the proper coordination and linkages of the responsible agencies in executing their roles provided herein. 5. Data Modernization. It shall relevant information submitted to them by the responsible agencies gathered in the course of executing their roles. The data shall be used to conduct situation analysis in order to formulate supplemental measures and strategies to further enhance and strengthen protection of children against sexual abuse. A systematic approach shall be established. Thus, the following mechanisms may be considered. a) Establish a Profiling System from the information submitted to them by the responsible agencies. b) Establish and maintain a master list and database of children all-over the city. The SOCC shall coordinate with the barangays and concerned agencies for the regular submission of relevant child-related information. These records pertaining to the information given to them shall be confidential and shall only be disclosed to proper authorities. c) Utilize the data gathered and provide a Situation Assessment and Analysis on Children relative to protection of children against sexual abuse. It shall also determine who are the children considered at a high-risk of being sexually abused and provide recommendations and action plans thereof to the Committee. The Situation Analysis can be used to identiff who are the children considered at a high-risk of being sexually abused and determine the risk factors and conditions that contribute to the incident such as: i. Risky behaviors of the perpetrator; ii. Handicapped victims or children with disabilities; iii. Povefi-stricken families; iv. Out-of-school youth; v. Dysfunctional households and abusive parents; vi. Those who live in isolated and/or far-flung remote communities; and vii. Other risk factors and conditions. d) As an end-product, provide a Local State of Children Report policy proposals and guidelines on how to address the situation and provide better protection for children against all forms of sexual abuse. e) The repoft shall be submitted to the Offlce of the City Mayor for any purpose it may deem proper. 6. Ensuring the functionality of programs and interuentions. It shall conduct periodic assessment regarding the programs and interuentions provided by responsible agencies. Identify the gaps existing therein and determine which programs and interuentions are non-functioning or has overlapping functions and those which are ineffective, inefficient and needs reconsideration, and provide remedies thereto. Ord. No. 0854-22, It must ensure that these programs and interuentions are age-appropriate, gender-sensitive and culturally-appropriate. It shall always provide utmost consideration to the best interest of the child. 7. Initiating Partnership with other agencies. ,It shall have the initiative to tap additional workforce and advocates for children protection such as Nongovernment Organizations (NGOs), Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), Faithbased Organizations and other volunteers and invite them to have joint effofts in combating sexual abuse on children. B. Other functions. Perform such other functions necessary to achieve the objectives of this Ordinance. ROLE OF CrrY TNFORMATTON OFFTCE (CrO)

text: RAISING AWARENESS ON CHILDREN PROTECTION AGAINST SEXUAL ABUSE. The City Information Office (CIO) shall have the following duties and responsibilities: 1. It shall led the conduct of various advocacy, campaign and awareness-raising activities on the issue of sexual abuse on children. With this, a representative from CIO shall serue as the Communication Specialist who shall ensure efficient and effective delivery of information. Pursuant to Proclamation No. 731, SERIES of 1996, the CIO shall take an active paft and enjoin the commemoration of 'tNational Awareness Week for the Prevention of Child Sexual Abuse and Exploitation". The CIO shall also take an active role in raising awareness of the global celebration of "Safer Internet Day" (SID) and call upon all stakeholders to join together to make the internet a safer and better place for all, especially for children and young people. 2. Ensure that persons responsible for the activities must be well-oriented with the laws, including this Ordinance, providing for protection to children against sexual abuse and should also have the capacity to communicate and explain it to the persons in their target area. 3. Ensure that the effectiveness of the activities, taking into account the language, dialect and over-all literacy of the intended audience. 4. The activities to be conducted must be strategically implemented. To ensure efficient allocation of resources, the CIO should prioritize the places with high risk of sexual abuse on children as well as in places where children at high-risk are usually located. 5. Ensure the adequacy of the information to be disseminated especially emphasizing on the rights of the children against sexual abuse. Also, it shall emphasize the duties of the stakeholders such as Government through its responsible agencies, non-government organizations, the family and relatives of the child, teachers and other school personnel and other persons having a role in capacitating the local community in giving children protection against sexual abuse. ; Ord. No. 0854-22 6. Ensure a captive-audience in implementing the activities. With the advent of social media, the CIO shall also optimize the mainstream of social media spaces to popularize the campaign against sexual abuse on children. 7. Ensure that hotlines and other venues for reporting incidents of sexual abuse are posted in conspicuous places including social media. 8. Perform such other functions necessary to raise awareness on children protection against sexual abuse and achieve the objectives of this Ordinance. ROLE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION (DEPED)

text: SCHOOL-BASED PROGRAMS. The Depaftment of Education (DepEd), through its Division Office and in coordination with the Child Protection Committee (CPC) created within the school, shall aid in strengthening children protection against sexual abuse through the following measures and strategies: 1. Conduct various advocacies, campaigns and other forms of information dissemination activities for purposes of raising awareness on children protection against sexual abuse in a school-setting. The Division Office may coordinate with the City Information Office for purposes of implementing this provision. 2. Formulate and implement child protection policies, guidelines and procedures for quick response and appropriate referral system for purposes of enhancing and strengthening child protection and safety against sexual abuse in a school-setting. 3. In coordination with CSWDO and SOCC, conduct training for teachers and other school personnel relating to protection of children against sexual abuse in a school-setting such as: a. Equipping them with the ability to recognize potential indicators of sexual abuse incidents among the students; b. Equipping them with the ability to influence children in mentally conditioning them on how to protect themselves from the vices of sexual abuse and their vulnerability to it. They shall aid in building resiliency, self-esteem and psychological competence of students against sexual abuse through providing them appropriate information knowledge and skills; c. Conduct training in handling incidents of sexual abuse committed to students speciflcally on repofting to appropriate agencies including referral to rehabilitation centers, providing comfoft to victims and maintaining the confidentiality thereof; d. Ensure that they are well-oriented with laws relating to sexual abuse, including this Ordinance, and determine their duties and the rights of the students embodied therein; e. Members of the Committee on Decorum and Investigation (CODI) and other officers created pursuant to Safe Spaces City Ordinance of Davao City shall participate in the training and be equipped with competence to handle cases of sexual abuse involving children; Ord. No. 0854-22 4. Develop and incorporate in the curriculum of the children in public or private schools with information that will enable them to understand the vices of sexual abuse and their vulnerability to it and mentally condition in them the necessity to protect themselves from it. Also, develop age-appropriate, gender-sensitive and cultural-appropriate information materials relating to protection of children against sexual abuse. The DepEd, in coordination with IGDD and CSWDO, shall provide Child Protection Policy Modules to fufther strengthen the city's child protection program and empower children to seek protection against abusers. Encourage the students to provide anti-sexual abuse activities to be included in the plans of the student government/councils, clubs or organizations, cocurricular activities and other school-based programs; 5. Establish a Master list and Database on Students where records pertaining to the information of students shall be kept confidentially; 6. Provide a Situation Assessment and Analysis to determine who are those students that are considered at high-risk of being sexually abused. The Situation Analysis can be used to determine the school-based risk factors and conditions that contribute to incidents of sexual abuse on children. It shall also give recommendations to the Committee necessary to enhance and strengthen the protection of children against sexual abuse. 7. Ensure that hotlines and other venues for repofting incidents of sexual abuse are posted in the conspicuous premises of the school. 8. It shall serue as repository of information related to sexual abuse in schoolsetting and shall maintain reports of incidents and cases of all schools. The records shall be confidential and only upon the request of proper agencies such as the Committee, courts, police and others that the same shall be disclosed. 9. Provide for other mechanisms that will fufther enhance and strengthen protection of children against sexual abuse and develop a safe and protective environment. The provisions laid down in DepEd Order No. 40, SERIES of 20t2, shall apply herein suppletorily. ROLE OF CTTY SOCIAL WELFARE AND DEVELOPMENT OFFICE (CSWDO)

The CSWDO shall also conduct life-skill trainings to the members of the family. a) Children should be able to learn life-skills against all forms of sexual abuse such as, but not limited to, the following: Recognition skills - A child should be able to determine sexual invitations and innuendos of the perpetrator. He or she should also be able to identify risk indicators such as when he or she is isolated with a stranger. Fufther, he or she should become more cautious and vigilant in the place and people around him or her. Communication skills - Knowing how to refuse sexual invitations and innuendos of the perpetrator. Practical and feasible self-defense skills - it may tap the DCPO or other agencies with competency to provide such skills. Repofting skills - A child should be guided where to report incidents and seek aid. These may include parents, relatives, teachers, barangay officials, police officers, and hotlines. That if he or she is threatened, the child should be able to know how he/she can seek assistance and whom he or she can approach. b) Parents and other persons with parental authority shall be equipped with skills appropriate for protecting the child from any forms of sexual abuse such as, but not limited to, the following: iv t ii. iii i. text: RESCUE, REHABILITATION AND SOCIAL REINTEGRATION SERVICES. -The CSWDO shall provide rescue, rehabilitation and social reintegration seruices for children who are victims of sexual abuse. 1. It shall provide the child-victims therapeutic interuentions to overcome the negative effects of sexual abuse; 2. It shall provide child-victims temporary shelters, counseling, psycho-social seruices and/or, recovery, rehabilitation programs and livelihood assistance; 3. It shall provide rehabilitative counseling and treatment to Children in Conflict with the Law (CICL) towards learning constructive ways of coping with sexually abusive behaviors and reforming their ways. When necessary, the offender shall be submitted to psychiatric treatment or confinement; 4. It shall provide social reintegration seruices to those considered as Children in Conflict with the Law (CICL) who are alleged as, accused of, or adjudged as having committed sexual abuse under Philippine laws; 5. Ensure that sufficient number of social workers are equipped with competence to handle cases of sexual abuse involving children. Moreover, it shall ensure that the social workers are well-oriented with laws relating to sexual abuse including this Ordinance for purposes of determining their duties and identifying the rights of the children embodied therein. Children subject to rescue, rehabilitation and social reintegration programs shall include those who are victims of child prostitution. This should be able to help responsible agencies to determine where to give priority in providing protection seruices and interuentions; ii. Ord. No. 0854-22 c) Ensure that the programs shall reach the far-flung or hard-to-reach areas by strengthening coordinative mechanism with responsible agencies; d) Monitor the proper implementation of the laws and programs related to protection of children against sexual abuse including the provisions of this Ordinance; e) Establish a Masterlist and Database on Children where records peftaining to the information of children in the barangay which shall be kept confidentially and shall only be disclosed to appropriate persons or agencies; 0 Provide a Situation Assessment and Analysis on Children relative to the protection of children against sexual abuse. The BCPC shall lead in capacitating the Barangay to quickly respond to sexual abuse on children through the following measures and strategies. 1. Ensure that hotlines and other venues for repofting incidents of sexual abuse are posted in the conspicuous place of the barangay including social media. 2. Coordinate with the Barangay to establish a Quick-Response Team for purposes of receiving complaints, immediate apprehension of perpetrators caught in flagrante delicto and referral to proper authorities such as DCPO. It may coordinate with existing barangay auxiliary units, Barangay Anti-Sexual Harassment Enforcers and Responders (BASHER) and other volunteer organizations. 3. text: ROLE OF DCPO. The Davao City Police Office (DCPO) shall have the following duties and responsibilities: 1. Its Women and Children Protection Desk (WCPD) shall be responsible for receiving repofts of incidents of sexual abuse involving children as well as referrals to it by responsible agencies; 2. During initial investigation, it shall determine whether the case involves a Child in Conflict with the Law (CICL). In such case, the provisions of Republic Act No. 9344 shall apply suppletorily. 3. It must ensure that the reception center for WCPD has a child-friendly atmosphere and officers responsible therein are equipped with skills necessary to handle cases involving children. t Ord. No. 0854-22 The officers assigned in such helpdesks must be equipped with the skills, information, and sensitivity to meet the needs of the victim as they often are the first to have contact with the child victim and his/her family. The DCPO, in coordination with SOCC, shall establish an education and training program for its police officers and barangay officials to enable them to properly handle cases of violence against women and their children. 4. It shall establish readily-available venues for reporting incidents such as, but not limited to, police hotlines, social media apps and others. The CSSDO, in coordination with the Special Office for Children's Concerns (SOCC) which created the Kean Gabriel Hotline, shall coordinate with the DCPO with regard to reports received which involve sexual abuse on children. 5. In rescue operations for children, the personnel must be accompanied by the presence of at least one (1) social worker, but the case must still be indorsed to a government social worker aftenruards. 6. It shall coordinate with social workers as to the treatment, rehabilitation, and social reintegration of the child/children victim. 7. It shall also provide necessary seruices or referral to appropriate institutions and agencies to address the medical, psychological, legal and other practical needs of the child-victim and/or child-perpetrator. It may tap the seruices of the City Health Office (CHO), Public Attorney's Office (PAO) and other appropriate agencies.

text: RATIONALE AND CONSIDERATIONS FOR ESTABLISHING A LOCALIZED CICC. The rationale and considerations for establishing a localized CICC are as follows: 1. The creation of CICC of Davao City as well as its composition and functions was inspired from the creation of Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) under Republic Act No. 10175 or the "Cybercrime Prevention Act of 20t2". Hence, the functions and responsibilities are already existing as well as the tools, machineries and expertise of personnel. 2. In this proposed Ordinance, it aims to localize the functions of CICC under RA 10175 and took consideration of the following criteria: Ord. No. 0854-22 a. The provisions were tailored to address online sexual abuse on children; b. In contrast with the National CICC, the localized version of CICC will tend to put more focus on addressing the sexual abuse on children within the city taking into consideration the specific attributable factors and conditions existing within the city. c. It will hopefully magnify the efforts in combating sexual abuse against children since the effofts to be rendered are more isolated and focused in the city compared to the general overuiew of national CICC. d. The specific local agencies involved are hereby determined. e. The coordination and linkages among the local CICC to the national and international on intelligence, investigations, training and capacity building are hereby established; f. The proposed localized CICC is hereby tasked to aid the Committee on Children Protection against sexual abuse specifically in combating online sexual abuse; ROLE OF MASS MEDIA

text: MEDIA HANDLING OF NEWS AND ISSUES INVOLVING CHILDREN.- Pursuant to Republic Act No. 9344, the mass media shall play an active role in the promotion of child rights, and delinquency prevention by relaying consistent messages through a balanced approach. Media practitioners shall, therefore, have the duty to maintain the highest critical and professional standards in repofting and covering cases of children in conflict with the law. In all publicity concerning children, the best interest of the child should be the primordial and paramount concern. Any undue, inappropriate and sensationalized publicity of any case involving a child in conflict with the law is hereby declared a violation of the child's rights. Further, pursuant to SECTION 23, Article II of Davao City Children's Welfare Code, as Amended, children in need of special protection shall not be exposed to undue media coverage unless consented to by the child and parent/guardian. The component authorities shall undertake all measures to protect this confidentiality of proceedings, including non-disclosure of records to the media, maintaining a separate police blotter for cases involving Children in Conflict with the Law which shall not be used in subsequent proceedings for cases involving the same offender as an adult, except when beneficial for the offender and upon his/her written consent. text: - The City of Davao shall ensure that its culture and tradition is appreciated, promoted and preserved. text: MANDATORY WEARING OF IP AND MORO INSPIRED ATTIRE - It shall be required for all City government employees in the City of Davao to wear an Indigenous Peoples Inspired Attire or Moro Inspired Attire and/or accessories based on the eleven (11) tribes of Davao City, every first Monday of the month to celebrate the local culture. City government employees who belong to any of the eleven (11) tribes in Davao City can likewise wear their authentic attire. City government employees whose ethnicity is outside the domain of the eleven (11) tribes of Davao City, may likewise wear their respective ethnic attire. This shall be required for all city government employees, whether holding casual, contractual, hold-over, permanent and/or temporary capacity.
title: Ordinance No. 086-22

text: EXCEPTIONS - The following acts or employees shall be exempted from the implementation of this Ordinance: 7.1 Those who are regularly peforming their duties and functions in the field, and those assigned in actual field operations; 7.2 When the nature of the work of the concerned employee demands that he or she wears a clothing other than what is imposed in this Ordinance; 7.3 Those who are prohibited to wear such attire by reason of their religious affiliation; 7.4 Those employees who have lost a loved one may wear their mourning clothes during their period of mourning; and 7.5 Pregnant female employees who need to wear their maternity clothes. M - An Indigenous People or Moro inspired attire is appropriate when it does not diminish the value of the cultural heritage of the Indigenous People of the Moro tribes of the City. A prescribed pattern shall be incorporated to the inspired attire as approved by the eleven tribes, to be worn by the City govemment employees, such as but not limited to, their uniforms or office-issued shifts. The eleven (11) tribes shall likewise prescribe the accessories that may be worn by the City government employees, in lieu of the inspired attire. This prescribed pattern and/or accessory are those commonly known to be used or are representation of each of the eleven tribes in Davao City, as approved by their Council leaders to be correct and appropriate in accordance with their tradition and practice.

text: DECLARATION OF PRINCIPLES AND POLICIES A. The City Government of Davao is committed to building and maintaining a peaceful society where its citizens have the capacity to lead long, happy lives which is ultimately the goal of all development. Peacebuilding should therefore be a cross-cutting theme in any development plan or program. Peacebuilding is the process of increasing connectors and decreasing dividers so that equitable development can occur. On the other hand, development is the process of increasing capacities and decreasing vulnerabilities so that people's choices are expanded to enable them to lead long happy lives. B. There are eight broad categories that create and sustain peaceful societies. The Institute for Economics and Peace has identified the following eight (B) Pillars of Positive Peace as the most common characteristics of most peaceful societies. These pillars are: . well-functioning government; . low levels of corruption; o dcc€ptance of the rights of others; o good relations with neighbors; o SoUr.ld business environment; . high levels of human capital; . equitable distribution of resources; and . free flow of information. The concept of Positive Peace acknowledges that ending direct violence alone does not guarantee durable peace. Ending direct violence is Negative Peace. For peace to endure, a society must build longer-term conditions that enable society to unify and flourish. This is called Positive Peace. Investing in Positive Peace improves resilience, mitigates risk of violence, and reduces the economic toll from conflict. The Eight Pillars of Positive Peace are highly interconnected and interact together to build a system. It therefore requires building capacities for peace not only of the government but also of local communities and other structures and institutions of the City. The establishment of Peace 911-The Center for Peacebuilding will contribute to the achievement of the t7 Sustainable Development Goals of the United Nations, in pafticular Goal 16 on building peace, justice and strong institutions, strengthening human rights, reducing discrimination and inequality, promoting gender equality, preseruing natural resources and protecting the climate. title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTIONALIZTNG THE ALTERNATIVE LEARNING SYSTEM (ALS) IN THE CITY OF DAVAO, PROVTDING GUIDELINES THEREOF, ALLOCATING FUNDS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES ABSENT: 1' *r'

text: DECLARATION OF POLICY - It shall be the policy of the Local Government of Davao to seek organized means and systematic methods of institutionalizing the Alternative Learning System (ALS). Towards this end, the City shall provide out-of-school children in special cases and adults with oppoftunities to improve their knowledge, values, life skills, and readiness for higher education, work or self-employment through a system of non-formal or indigenous education, or both which are tailored to respond to their learning needs and life circumstances. The City shall also ensure the close paftnership and collaboration with the barangays and private sectors.
title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTIONALIZTNG THE ALTERNATIVE LEARNING SYSTEM (ALS) IN THE CITY OF DAVAO, PROVTDING GUIDELINES THEREOF, ALLOCATING FUNDS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES ABSENT: 1' *r'

text: OBJECTMS This Ordinance aims to achieve the following objectives: a. Provide adequate, timely and quality attention and suppoft to the basic learning needs of out-of-school children in special cases and adults including indigenous people; b, Guarantee equitable access for all learners, including those who reside in the unreached, underserued, conflict-affected communities and communities in emergency situations to avail of systematic, flexible and appropriate alternative basic education program outside of the formal school system; d. Hire, capacitate, and deploy ALS Teachers, Community ALS Implementors and Learning Facilitators to deliver a range of ALS programs especially in far-flung, unserued, underserued, conflict-affected communities, and communities in emergency situations; e. Design specialized programs for learners with disabilities, taking into consideration their different levels of learning needs and other functional difficulties in the development of instructional materials and learning resources in accessible format; t. Develop, integrate, and utilize non-formal and informal education approaches and strategies in the delivery of the ALS programs and the assessment of learning outcomes and competencies of ALS learners by providing flexibility in the duration of learning programs, learning contents, and delivery strategies, among others; g. Improve access education and other learning oppoftunities and raise the level of literacy to contribute to an individual's sustainable future; and c. Promote lifelong learning oppoftunities anchored on the Alternative Learning System (ALS), K to 12 Basic Education Curriculum (BEC) that takes a holistic, integrated and inter-sectoral approach, and provide pathways across modes of learning which will ensure that learners will become caring, self-reliant, independent, productive and patriotic citizens, by allowing such learners to pursue further education, after pafticipating in the ALS program and passing the accreditation and equivalency assessments or ceftifications, or both required by the Depaftment of Education (DepEd), or seek employment; i i i Ord. No. 0893-22 h. Strengthen non-formal basic education programs while ensuring suppoft to the policy of the DepEd that school age children should be enrolled in formal education, and that they should be able to return to the formal education system in the event that they drop out.
title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTIONALIZTNG THE ALTERNATIVE LEARNING SYSTEM (ALS) IN THE CITY OF DAVAO, PROVTDING GUIDELINES THEREOF, ALLOCATING FUNDS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES ABSENT: 1' *r'

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - For purposes of this Ordinance, the following shall mean: a. Alternative Learning System K to 12 Basic Education Curriculum (ALS K to 12 BEC) - shall refer to the comprehensive curriculum indicating the competency, content, key stages, and standards for the ALS program under this Ordinance. The ALS K to 12 BEC is benchmarked on the DepEd formal school curriculum and focuses on the 21st Century Skills, information, media and technology skills, learning and innovation skills, communication skills, and life and career skills. b. Alternative Learning System Teacher (ALS Teacher) - shall refer to DepEd employed teachers who implement the ALS program. c. Adult - shall refer to a person at least eighteen (18) years of age and above. d. Alternative Learning Sytem (ALS) - shall refer to a parallel learning system that provides a viable alternative to the existing formal education instruction. It encompasses both non-formal and informal source of knowledge and skills. e. Basic Literacy Program - shall refer to the program component of ALS that is aimed at eradicating illiteracy among out-of-school children in special cases and adults by developing basic literacy skills of reading, writing, numeracy, and simple comprehension. f. Community Alternative Learning System Implementors (Community ALS Implementors) - shall refer to persons engaged either by the Depaftment of Education or any Local Government Unit (LGU) to deliver ALS programs to out-of-school children in special cases and adults. g. Community Learning Center (CLC) - shall refer to a physical space to house learning resources and facilities of a learning program for out-ofschool children in special cases and adults. It is a venue for a face-to-face learning activities and other learning oppoftunities for community development and improvement of the people's quality of life. h. Indigenous Peoples (IP) - refer to a group of people of homogenous societies identified by self-ascription and ascription by others, who have continuously lived as organized community on communally bounded and defined territory, and who have under claims of ownership since time immemorial, occupied, possessed and utilized such territories, sharing common bonds of language, customs, tradition and other distinctive culture traits or who have, through resistance to political, social and cultural inroads of colonization became historically differentiated from the majority of the Filipinos. Ord. No. 0893-22 i. Indigenous Peoples Education - shall refer to the program that supports education initiatives undeftaken through formal, non-formal, and informal modalities with emphasis on any of, but not limited to, the key areas of indigenous knowledge systems and practices and community history, indigenous language, Indigenous Learning System (ILS), and community life cycle-based curriculum and assessment, educational goals, aspirations and competencies specific to the Indigenous Cultural Community (ICC), engagement of elders and other community members in the teachinglearning process, assessment, and management of the initiative, recognitional and continuing practice of the community's ILS, and the rights and responsibilities of ICCs. j. Informal Education - shall refer to diverse forms of learning that are international or deliberate but are not institutionalized. It is a lifelong process of learning by which every person acquires and accumulates knowledge, skills, attitudes and insights from daily experiences at home, at work, at play and from life itself towards literacy. k. Learners with Disabilities - shall refer to those who have long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which in interaction with various barriers may hinder their full and effective participation in society on equal basis with others. l, Learning Facilitators - shall refer to teachers financed by the private sector who implement ALS programs. The private sector shall include nongovernment organizations or associations, civic society organizations, or individuals. m. Micro-Ceftification, also known as micro-credentialing - shall refer to a flexible means of certifying attainment of specific elements of ALS K to 12 minimum competencies which can be used by the holder as credential such as in job application, recruitment and selection. n. Non-Formal Education (NFE) shall refer to any organized and systematic educational activity carried outside the framework of the formal education system to provide selected types of learning to a segment of the population. o. Out-of-School Children in Special Cases - shall refer to children of official school age who are not enrolled in the elementary or secondary schools due to special cases such as economic, geographic, political, cultural, or social barriers, including learners with disabilities or conditions, indigenous peoples, children in conflict with the law, learners in emergency situations, and other marginalized sectors.
title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTIONALIZTNG THE ALTERNATIVE LEARNING SYSTEM (ALS) IN THE CITY OF DAVAO, PROVTDING GUIDELINES THEREOF, ALLOCATING FUNDS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES ABSENT: 1' *r'

text: ALS PROGRAM - The City Government shall coordinate with the Department of Education (DepEd) to strengthen the implementation of a range of priority NFE programs including, but not limited to, the following: a. Basic Literary Program; b. A&EPrograms; c. Indigenous Peoples Education Program; d. Academic-Focused Bridging Programs; and e. Functional Education and Literacy Programs Ord. No. 0893-22 To effectively deliver the NFE programs, the city government may utilize appropriate, relevant and responsive learning modalities but not limited to the following: a. text: DEFINITION OF TERMS As used in this Ordinance the following terms shall mean: a. text: DECLARATION OF POLICY - It is hereby declared that Davao City recognizes tourism as an indispensable component of the Clty's socio-economic development. This Ordinance intends to: a) provide measures that will position Davao City as a top desired destination for regional, national, and international Meetings, Incentives, Conventions, and Exhibitions (MICE); b) enact policies that will strengthen the Meetings, Incentives, Conventions, and Exhibitions (MICE) industry in the City; and c) set the direction of the Meetings, Incentives, Conventions, and Exhibitions (MICE) industry; SECTIOI{ 3. A non-business vacation with the aim of continued motivation for performance. Incentives may include incentive travel or trip. e) Conventions are events that have specific objectives and exchanges of information. 0 Exhibitions are those where displayed products or services are the event's primary focus.

WETLANDS - an ecosystem flooded by water, permanently or seasonally. It includes areas where water covers the soil, or is present either at or near the sudace of the soil saturating the area. text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - For purposes of this Ordinance, the following terms are defined: 2.1 Percons with Disability (PWDs) are defined by Republic Act No.7277 or the Magna Cafta fior Disabled Persons as persons suffering from restriction of different abilities, as a result of a mental, physical or sensory impairment, to peform an activity in the manner or within the range considered normal for a human being. An impairment is any loss, diminution or aberration of psychological, physiological, or anatomical structure of function. Disability shall mean (1) physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more psychologica!, physiological or anatomical function of an individual or activities of such individual; (2) a record of such an impairment; or (3) being regarded as having such an impairment. Persons designated by law as PWDs, such as Cancer Survivors pursuant to Republic Act No. 11215 or the National Integrated Cancer Control Act, persons with Rare Diseases under Republic Act No. LA747 or the Rare Diseases Act of the Philippines, and other related laws shall be considered as PWDs. 2.2 A Cinema or Movie theater is a venue, usually a building or located within malls, that contains seating for an audience for the purpose of public enteftainment. It is a commercial operation that plays films or movies fur paying customers. 2.3 PWD ldentification Card (PWD ID)refers to the official Identification Cards issued by the City Govemment of Davao to persons classified as PWDs. It shall bear the name, picture and type of disability of the PWD; 2.4 Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) refers to a company's voluntary - commitment to conduct business in an ethical way, and to contribute to the development of society and the local communrty. SECTIOil 3. GUIDELINES AND REGULATIOilS - The following acts shall be obserued in the implementation of this Ordinance: 3.1 FREE MOVIE PRMIEGE. Persons with Disability with duly issued PWD IDs shall enjoy the privilege of free movie access to any film of their choice, in a cinema or movie theater. The free movie privilege shall be non-transferable and may only be availed of by the PWD. If the PWD cannot personally transact with cinema personnel, he/she may be represented by his/her companion for transaction purposes, provided, they are present during the transaction. Cinemas or cinema operators Ord. No.0155-23 must strictly implement a 'NO PWD ID, NO ENTRY" policy. The PWD must also present his/her movie pass booklet upon entry. The free movie privilege only applies to regular movie screenings, excluding specialcinemas such as Dolby Atmos, IM$(Theaters, Dirccb/s Club, and 3D and 4D theaters. For blockbuster films, the ftee movie privilege may only be availed of during its second week. The said privilege does not extend to screenings for special events such as sponsored movie premierc, pay-per-view shows, and the like. 3.2 MOVIE PASS BOOKLET. The Persons with Disabilities Affairs ffice (PDAO) shall issue availing PWDs with a Movie Pass Booklet. The said booklet shall contain the serial number, PWDs full name, photo, address, PWD ID number, and signature. The booklet shall also contain the dates and number of movies that the PWD may avail of during the entire year. The movie pass booklet shall be non-transferable and must be presented by the PWD to the cinema personnel upon entry. 3.3 VERIFICATIOII. For purposes of verification of PWD IDs, Cinema Operators must refer to the Philippine Registry for Person with Disability Website (PRPWD). Should cinema operators wish to conduct fufther verificaUon, they may also contact the Records SECTION of the City Social Welfare and Development ffice (CSWDO) at (082) 286-3689. 3.4 AVAILMEilT. The free movie pass may be availed of only by Pl/tlDs registered under the City Government of Davao. They may avail of the free movie privilege once a week, every Monday, and during the first screening only. However, cinemas are not prohibited fiom offering the ftee movie privilege on additional days of the week. The free movie pass is good for one screening only per week. Should the PWD opt to screen another movie on the scheduled ftee movie privilege day, they will have to pay the regular movie entrance with the 20olo discount provided for under the law. 3.5 PARTICIPATING CINEMAS. The Memorandum of Agreement shall provide the specific day and time when the privilege may be availed of, the allotrnent of seats for PWDs, and the proof of identification rcquired to be presented to avail of the free movie access in the available movie theaters of the cinema operators. i.. Ord. No.0155-23 The free movie privilege granted to PV1/Ds under this Ordinance shall be counted under the cinema's Corporate Social Responsibility program. 3.7 MONITORING SHEET. Cinema owners and operators must provide a monthly monitoring sheet where the PWDs will register their full name, signature, and PWD ID number upon availing of the privilege. All cinemas within the jurisdiction of the City of Davao are required to display posters or notices on the cinema booths where cinema viewers transact to buy tickets. text: DECLARATION OF POLICY - The Local Government of Davao City acknowledges the mandate of the 1987 Philippine Constitution pafticularly Article II, SECTION D(, which states that "The State shall adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development which shall endeavor to make essenUal goods, trealth, and other social seruices available to all people at affordable cost. There shall be priority for the needs of the underprivileged, sick, elderly, disabled, women and children". Fufthermore, Republic Act No. 9994 or the "Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 20L0' provides that a Healthy and Productive Ageing Program for senior citizens shall be provided. This program prinrarily ainrs to promote quality life anrong older persons and contribute to nation building through providing equitable access to quality healthcare.
