text: IIIE - This Ordinance shall be known as "THE ANTI-BULLYING ORDINANCE OF DAVAO CITY.'
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: POUCY DECLARATION - It is hereby declared the policy of the City of Davao to ensure that the fundamental rights of persons to life, liberty, property, and security are promoted and protected. As a society composed of persons, the City recognizes the impoftance of individuality and the free exercise thereof as an essential ingredient of a well-functioning democracy. The practice of bullying, however, shall be met with disdain as it is a form of abuse which serves to deprive others of the free exercise of their own rights. In consonance with the national government's poliry under Republic Act No. 10627 declaring acts of bullying as unacceptable, Republic Act No. 11313 where both men and women must be safe and secure not only in private but also in public spaces, online, workplaces, and educational institutions, and other pertinent national laws, all forms of bullying shall not be countenanced.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: ACTS OF BULLYING -"Bullying" as adopted from Republic Act No. 10627, shall refer to any severe or repeated act by one or more persons through a written, verbal or electronic expression, or a physical act or gesture, or any combination thereof, directed at another individual that has the effect of actually causing or placing the latter in reasonable fear of physical or emotional harm to himself or damage to his propefi; creating a hostile environment at the schoo!, workplace, or any other situation for the individual; infringing on the rights of the individual; or materially and substantially disrupting the education process or the orderly operation of a school, workplace, or any other area, venue, or situation; such as, but not limited to, the following: a) Any unwanted physical contact between the bully and the complainant, such as punching, pushing, shoving, kicking, slapping, tickling, headlocks, inflicting pranks, teasing, fighting and the use of available objects as weapons; b) Any act that causes damage to an individual's psyche and/or emotional well-being; c) Any slanderous statement or accusation that causes an individual undue emotional distress, such as directing foul language or profanity at the target, name-calling, tormenting and commenting negatively on an individual's looks, clothes and body; d) Cyberbullying or any bullying done through the use of technology or any electronic means. Bullying shall be further classified into four (4) aspects, namely: a. Bullying in educational institutions b. Bullying in the workplace c. Cyberbullying d. Bullying in other public places Any person who commits the acts described above is considered a bully. Persons who, through the acts described above, retaliate against another person who repofts acts of bullying or who provides information during an investigation or is a witness under such investigation, shall also be considered to have committed bullying. Ord. No. 0L92-23
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: ACTS OF BULLYING Iil EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS - RefeT to any severe, or repeated use by one or more students of a written, verbal or electronic expression, or a physical act or gesture, or any combination thereof, directed at another student that has the effect of actually causing or placing the latter in reasonable fear of physical or emotional harm or damage to his propefi; creating a hostile environment at school for the other student; infringing on the rights of another student at school; or materially and substantially disrupting the education process or the orderly operation of a school, such as, but not limited to, the following: 1. Any unwanted physical contact between the bully and the victim like punching, pushing, shoving, kicking, slapping, tickling, headlocks, inflicting school pranks, teasing, fighting and the use of available objects as weapons; 2. Any act that causes damage to a victim's psyche and/or emotional well-being; 3. Any slanderous statement or accusation that causes the victim undue emotional distress like directing foul language or profanity at the target, name-calling, tormenting and commenting negatively on victim's looks, clothes and body. Educational institutions covered under this Ordinance include public or private schools, regardless of educational level, such as: a) Preparatory schools; b) Primary schools; c) Secondary schools; d) Colleges and universities, including post-graduate; e) Vocational schools; 0 Review centers, tutorial centers, and other similar establishments; g) Training institutions by virtue of education such as On-the-Job training as well as other activities performed off-school, but for educational purpose/s. Persons liable for bullying under this SECTION include, but are not limited to, the following: i. Students; ii. Trainees, interns, exchange students, and volunteers; iii. Teachers, student-teachers and non-teaching staff; iv. School Administrators; v. Parents and guardians of students; vi. Other authorized persons within the school campus; vii. Visitors. All acts and repofts of bullying in the aforementioned institutions, and al! acts of bullying by, among, and between the aforementioned persons shall be under the primary jurisdiction of the educational institution concerned.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: ACTS OF BULLYING IN THE WORKPI-ACE. Acts of bullying in the workplace can be defined as the intentiona! and repeated less favorable treatment of a person by another or others in the workplace, which may be considered unreasonable and inappropriate workplace practice, but excludes acts which necessarily fall under management prerogative and discipline done in good faith and without violating employee rights. Management prerogative here refers to the employer's inherent right to regulate, according to his own discretion and judgment, all aspects of employment, including hiring, work assignments, working methods, the time, place and manner of work, work supervision, transfer of employees, lay-off of workers, discipline, dismissal, and recall of employees. Ord. No. 0L92-23 Workplace bullying includes, but is not limited to, behavior that intimidates, offends, degrades or humiliates a worker, possibly in front of co-workers, clients, customers, vendors, visitors, and other persons in a workplace setting or outside therof, by reason of such employment. Acts of bullying in the workplace include the acts previously enumerated under and other acts such as, but not limited to: a. Frequently intimidating or undermining employees by demeaning their work standards, not giving them credit, setting them up for failure, and reminding them of old mistakes; b. Uninterrupted threatening of employees' personal self-esteem and work status; c. Continuous isolation of employees from opportunities, information, and interaction with others; d. Repeatedly giving impossible deadlines, creating undue pressure and stress, and overworking employees; e. Giving constant and unfair criticism; f. Persistent blaming without factual justification; g. Frequently making unreasonable demands; h. Giving hostile glares and other intimidating gestures repeatedly; i. Constant yelling, screaming, and swearing; j. Purposely excluding or isolating a coworker repeatedly; k. Frequently sending aggressive emails or notes; l. Incessant monopolization of supplies and other resources; m. Persistently engaging in excessive social bantering, teasing, and humiliation; n. Deliberately insulting others and taking paft in behind-the-back put-downs repeatedly; o. Monitoring another excessively in a continuous manner; p. Repeatedly stealing credit for other employees'work, except when the nature of the work is collective or commissioned.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: CYBERLIBEL - Cyberlibel is the unlawful or prohibited acts of libel as defined in Afticle 355 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended, committed through a computer system or any other similar means which may be devised in the future. Computer system refers to any device or group of interconnected or related devices, one or more of which, pursuant to a program, performs automated processing of data. It covers any type of device with data processing capabilities including, but not limited to, computers and mobile phones. The device consisting of hardware and software may include input, output and storage components which may stand alone or be connected in a network or other similar devices. It also includes computer data storage devices or media.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: ADDRESSING BULLYING IN EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIOilS -All educationa! institutions are hereby directed to adopt policies to address the existence of bullying. Such policies shall be regularly updated and, at a minimum, shall include provisions which: A.Identify the range of disciplinary administrative actions that may be taken against a respondent for bullying or retaliation which shall be commensurate with the nature and gravity of the offense: Provided, that, in addition to the disciplinary sanctions imposed upon a respondent of bullying or retaliation, he/she shall also be required to undergo a rehabilitation program which shall be administered by the institution concerned. The parents of the said respondent shall be encouraged by the said institution to join the rehabilitation program. 'i Page 5 of 10. O'rd. No. 0L92-23. B. Establish clear procedures and strategies for: 1. Reporting acts of bullying or retaliation; 2. Responding promptly to and investigating reports of bullying or retaliation; 3. Restoring a sense of safety for a victim and assessing the student's need for protection; 4. Protecting from bullying or retaliation of a person who reports acts of bullying, provides information during an investigation of bullying, or is witness to or has reliable information about an act of bullying; and 5. Providing counseling or referral to appropriate services for respondents, complainants, and appropriate family members of said students. C.Enable students to anonymously report bullying or retaliation: Provided, however, that no disciplinary administrative action shall be taken against a respondent solely on the basis of an anonymous report; D.Subject a student who knowingly makes a false accusation of bullying to disciplinary administrative action; E. Educate students on the dynamics of bullying, the anti-bullying policies of the school as well as the mechanisms of such school for the anonymous reporting of acts of bullying or retaliation; F. Educate parents and guardians about the dynamics of bullying, the anti-bullying policies of the school and how parents and guardians can provide support and reinforce such policies at home; and G.Maintain a public record of relevant information and statistics on acts of bullying or retaliation in school: Provided, that the names of students who committed acts of bullying or retaliation shall be strictly confidential and only made available to the school administration, teachers directly responsible for the said students and parents or guardians of students who are or have been victims of acts of bullying or retaliation. All educational institutions shall provide students and their parents or guardians a copy of the anti-bullying policies being adopted by the school. Such policies shall likewise be included in the school's student and/or employee handbook and shall be conspicuously posted on the school walls and website, if there is any. Training programs, courses, or activities which shall provide opportunities for school administrators, teachers, and other employees to develop their knowledge and skills in preventing or responding to acts of bullying shall also be performed in these educational institutions.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: ADDRESSING BULLYING IN THE WORKPLACE - WOTKPIACCS are mandated to adopt anti-bullying policies as necessary in line with the demands of their industry. However, all public and private offices and establishments in the City are directed to also adopt the mandatory policies and guidelines issued by the Civil Seruice Commission (CSC), City Human Resources Management Office, and Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) in order to address bullying and other similar acts in the workplace. Workplaces categorized under the informal sector and those which do not require registration with DOLE are not covered under this SECTION and acts of bullying complained shill lnstead be considered as bullying in other public places as provided covered in the next succeeding SECTION. Ord. No. 0L92-23
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: BULLyIilG Iil OTHER PUBUC PTACES - This type of bullying covers those acts generally done outside of the educational institution or workplace, and also covers those acts done in a workplace as categorized under SECTION 8, paragraph 2.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: ADDRESSING BULLYING IN OTHER PUBLIC PLACES - IN order to address bullying in other public places, Anti-Bullying Desks (Desk) shall be created in all Barangays and/or District Centers in the city. The existing Women and Children Protection Desk Officers, Violence Against Women (VAW) Desk Officers, or their equivalent in the barangays shall also be empowered to act as Anti-Bullying Desk Officers. They shall be responsible for the enforcement of anti-bullying policies at the barangay level. Any person may report acts of bullying before the Desk in the Barangay where the offense was committed. The Desk shall have the authority to make a preliminary inquiry into the repofted case. Should the Desk determine that the act complained of is either in an educational institution or a workplace setting, the complaint shall be forwarded to the proper anti-bullying mechanism of the workplace or educational institution concerned. The Desk shall refer all proper identified cases of bullying under this SECTION to the Barangay Justice System of the barangay where the offense was committed. Every report of bulLying and any proceeding which concerns a minor shall at all times be represented and assisted by the legal guardian or next of kin, in the presence of a social worker or equivalent person. Every person who admits to or is found to have committed bullying under the Barangay Justice System shall be also be required to undergo a period of counseling and rehabilitation.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: RESOLUTION OF BULLYING CASES - Bullying cases shall be deemed resolved when: a. It has been determined with finality by the appropriate body that no act of bullying took place; b. There has been a settlement between the parties and the conditions of the same have been complied with; and c. There has been a determination that bullying has been committed, and the respondent(s), the complainant(s), and their immediate families have undergone the requisite disciplinary measures and rehabilitation/ interuention procedures, as may be provided in the concerned institution's internal mechanisms. When a case is deemed resolved, no liability under this Ordinance shall ensue. Non-resolution of cases may be considered a ground for Iiability under SECTION 19 of this Ordinance.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: CREATION OF A CITY ANTI-BULLYING COUNCIL - The City shall establish the City Anti-Bullying Council (CABC), which shall be responsible for the establishment of policies related to bullying. These policies shall include, among others, the formulation of necessary education, prevention, counseling and interuention measures. The CABC may, in the pefformance of its functions, request the list of bullying complaints from educational institutions, workplaces, and barangays, in order to effect the purposes of this Ordinance and of related national laws against bullying. The CABC shall convene regularly at least once a month. Ord. No. 0L92-23 All barangays, offices, committees, and bodies responsible for anti-bullying policies within their respective institutions and establishments are also required to submit to the CABC copies of these policies within one (1) year from the effectivity of this Ordinance. The CABC shall initially be composed of representatives from the following, and may be reconstituted as required under its internal rules: a. City Mayor - Chairperson b. City Social Welfare and Development Office - Vice-Chairperson/Secretariat c. SANGGUNIANG Panlungsod Committee on Civil, Political, and Human Rights - Member d. SANGGUNIANG Kabataan Federation - Member e. SANGGUNIANG Panlungsod Committee on Education, Science and Technology, Arts and Culture - Member f. Special Office for Children's Concerns - Member g. City Schools Superintendent/Depaftment of Education - Member h. Commission on Higher Education - Member i. Department of Labor and Employment - Member j. Davao City Police Office/Women and Children Protection - Member k. Philippine Mental Health Association - Member l. Liga ng mga Barangay Representative - Member m. Representative from Inter-faith Organizations/NG0 Representative - Member n. Representative from Medical Doctor from the Davao Medical Society - Member
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: CREATION OF CITY ANTI-BULLYING DESK - The City Anti-Bullying Desk (Desk) shall be created within any appropriate depaftment of the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO), and shall be responsible for the effective implementation of this Ordinance. The Desk shal! oversee the other Anti-Bullying Desks in Barangays and District Centers. The Desk shall also function as the secretariat of CABC, and shall handle the day-to-day affairs of the latter. The Desk is tasked to receive complainb of bullying in the city, and is empowered to forward cases to the proper forum for prompt disposition.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: CREATION OF AN ANTI.BULLYING HOTTINE . An antibullying telephone hotline shall be created, which shall entertain calls for reporting of instances of bullying, requests for assistance or rehabilitation, psychosocial suppoft, and other bullying-related concerns. This hotline shall be free of charge and shall maintain the privary and confidentiality of its callers. In addition to this telephone hotline, online chat or email accessibility shall also be established, obseruing the same level of privacy and confidentiality as its telephone counterpart.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: REHABILTTATION, INTERVENTION AND DTVERSION AND COUNSELING - An Interuention and Diversion program shall be designed for minor offenders who are held liable by the courts under this Ordinance. As for adults found liable, the Mental Health Division of the City Health Office (CHO) shall design and implement an appropriate counseling program.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: BULLYING PREVENTION MONTH - The month of October shall hereby be declared as the Davao City Bullying Prevention Month. During the said month, the City shall organize events and activities related to its anti-bullying policy. During this month, entities that are found compliant with the requisites for addressing bullying in their respective institutions shall be duly recognized and declared a Bullying-Free Establishment Ord. No. 0L92-23 SECTION L7. ADMINISTRATIVE LIABIUTY FOR INACTION OR NON - RESOLUTION OF CASES- Educational institutions and/or workplaces which fail to take action on repofts of bullying or fail to administratively resolve cases of bullying within their respective jurisdictions as required may be held liable as follows: a. First Offense: The educational institution and/or workplace concerned shal! be invited to appear before the CABC to explain the reason for the non- resolution within the required period. Should the explanation be found unjustifiable and/or unsatisfactory, the educational institution or workplace shall be cited for violation of this Ordinance and be subject to an administrative fine of FIVE THOUSAND PESOS (PhP5,000.00). b. Second Offense and Subsequent Offenses: Subsequent offenses by any educational institution and/or workplace shall warrant the payment of an administrative fine of FIVE THOUSAND PESOS (PhP5,000.00). The CABC may also recommend for the denial, for those entities required by law, of the application for renewal of the business permit issued by the Office of the City Mayor. The CABC shall further recommend to the proper authorities the filing of a complaint against the educational institution and/or workplace concerned, in accordance with pertinent substantive and procedural rules and relevant issuances of the Department of Education, the Commission on Higher Education (CHED), the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), the Civil Service Commission (CSC), the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), or any government agenry or instrumentality having jurisdiction over the entity being complained of, as may be applicable.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: PENALTIES - Persons at the age of majority who, having been administratively found to have committed acts of bullying or entered into settlement agreements in their respective forums, but willfully refuse or unjustifiably fail to comply with the conditions and penalties imposed upon him/her, shall be punished by imprisonment from three (3) to six (6) months and/or a fine ranging from THREE THOUSAND PESOS (PhP3,000.00) to FIVE THOUSAND PESOS (PhP5,000.00), at the discretion of the court. The aforementioned persons, whether a minor or an adult, shall also be required to enroll themselves into an appropriate intervention program which includes a combination of the following: a. Counseling for the perpetrator(s)/bully(ies), and in case of minors, including their parents or guardians, as the court may deem fit; b. Training, seminars and lectures on: i. Anger Management Skills; ii. Problem-solving and/or Conflict Resolution Skills; iii. Values Formation; and c. Payment for cost of treatment The program may be administered by duly licensed private therapists and counselors. For indigents, the court may direct the Mental Health Division to perform the necessary counseling.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: CONFIDENTIALITY OF RECORDS AND PROCEEDINGS - AII records and proceedings involving minors, from initial contact/reporting until the final decision of the case shall be considered privileged and confidential. The public shall be excluded during the proceedings and the records shall not be disclosed directly or indirectly to anyone by any of the parties or the participants in the proceedings for any purpose whatsoever. Parties privy to the proceedings are not allowed to disclose any information regarding any proceeding, unless for the purposes of proceedings which are under this Ordinance.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: IMPLEMENTING RULES AND REGULATIONS - The City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO), in conjunction with the CABC, shall take charge in the creation of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of this Ordinance within one hundred twenty (120) days after its effectivity.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: INFORMATION DISSEMINATION - A city-wide awareness campaign on the city's anti-bullying poliry, as encapsulated in this Ordinance, shall be implemented using tri-media, on-ground, and online platforms. Educational institutions are required to include the city's anti-bullying policy in their school orientations, school handbooks, and other information materials. Regular lectures on the prevention of bullying and other bullying-related topics shall be done in educational institutions and workplaces with the aid of organizations like the Philippine Mental Health Association and other similar entities.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: SUPPLETORY APPLICATION - Related existing laws on Anti-bullying and Mental Health such as RA No. 7877, or the Anti-Sexual Harassment Act of 1995; RA No. 9262, or the Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004; RA No. 11313, or the Safe Spaces Act, and other related laws, shall find suppletory application.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: Under SECTION 16, General Welfare Clause of the Loca! Government Code, Local Government Units are authorized to exercise the powers necessary, appropriate, or incidental to its efficient and effective governance and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare. Furthermore, under SECTION 2 of R.A. No. 10121, otherwise known as the Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010, the State aims to recognize the local risk patterns across the country, strengthen the capacity of LGUs for disaster risk reduction and management through decentralized powers, responsibilities, and resources at the regiona! and local levels, and strengthen the capacities of LGUs and communities in mitigating and preparing for, responding to, and recovering from the impact of disasters. Therefore, it is the declared policy of the City Government of Davao to protect the lives and propefties of its residents at all times, and, whenever possible, mitigate the effects of any man-made and natural disasters within its locality.

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - As used in this Ordinance, the following terms are hereby defined: (a) Accredited Community Disaster Volunteerc (ACDV) - are individuals or organized volunteers who possess the requisite qualifications, as stipulated in the guidelines currently utilized by CDRRMO, and whose names were submitted as officially included in the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Counci! (CDRRMC), List of Community Disaster Volunteers, and/or the National Roster of ACDVs maintained by the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) and have the following roles: Provide voluntary seruice to Local Government Units and communities for DRRM-related activities. ii. Ensure that services rendered are done in a professional manner and does not compromise the safety of the volunteers and communities they are assisting. (b) Community Volunteer Responderc (CVR) - a group of responders in the community that pedorm response activities. (c) Disaster - a serious disruption of the functioning of a community or a society involving widespread human, material, economic or environmental losses and impacts, which exceeds the ability of the affected community or society to cope using its own resources. For purposes of this Ordinance, disaster shall include both natural calamities and man-made disasters. (d) Disaster Prevention - the outright avoidance of adverse impacts of hazards and other related disasters. Page 3 of L2 Ord. No. 0246-23 (e) Disaster Victims - persons or group of persons who have been adversely affected by a natural or human-induced hazard who have to leave their habitual places of residence due to existing or impending threats, damaged shelter units, with casualty among immediate family members or those who remained in their habitual places of origin when still habitable but whose main source of income or livelihood had been damaged and are experiencing hopelessness and difficulty in coping or responding to the onslaught of the hazardous events on their own resources. (f) Early Warning System (EWS) - refers to the set of capacities needed to generate and disseminate timely and meaningful warning information to enable individuals, communities, and organizations threatened by a hazard to prepare and act appropriately and insufficient time to reduce the possibility of harm or loss. (g) Emergency an unforeseen or sudden occurrence, especially danger, demanding an immediate action. (h) Emergency Evacuation means an evacuation ordered by competent authoriW when an unforeseen disaster has suddenly occurred which requires immediate evacuation of the affected area/s. (i) Evacuation - means an operation whereby all or part of a particular population is temporarily relocated, whether individually or in an organized manner, from an area in which a disaster or emergenry has been declared and which is considered dangerous to the health and safety of the general public. g) Evacuation Area, Evacuation Center, or Evacuation Place - a place where the Disaster Victims, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and Vulnerable and Marginalized Groups are brought before, during,and after calamities or disasters such as, but not limited to, typhoons, floods, landslides, eafthquakes or fire, for care, safety and protection. (k) Hazard - a dangerous phenomenon, substance, human activity, or condition that may cause loss of life, injury or other health impacts, propefi damage, loss of livelihood and services, social and economic disruption, or environmental damage. (l) Imminent Danger - means any condition in any place such that a danger exists which could reasonably be expected to cause death or serious physical harm immediately upon or before the occurrence of any human-induced or natural disasters. (m) Indigenous Early Warning System (IEWS) - a community's traditional way of giving Early Warning, such as batingaw and observing animal behavior, celestial bodies, etc., in determining possible weather disturbances. Whatever works for the barangay is acceptable as long as the meaning and the recommended action are properly disseminated to the community and constantly practiced through the conduct of drills and other skills enhancement exercises. (n) Internally Displaced Percon (IDP) or Percons Displaced by the Disaster (PDP) - refers to persons or groups of persons who have been forced or obliged to flee or to leave their homes or places of habitual residence, in pafticular as a result of or in order to avoid the effects of natural or human-induced disasters, and who have not crossed an internationally recognized State border. Page 4 of L2 Ord. No. 0246-23 (b) Preemptive Evacuation - means an evacuation ordered as a resoft when a disaster has been declared and danger or loss of life is imminent, and conditions exist that may critically imperi! or endanger the lives of those in a defined area. (p) Public Aleft and Warning System (PAWS) - a system used to give warning to the public, such as a Siren, to alert the public of impending disaster occurrence. PAWS is usually science-based technology and mostly, those that are state-of-the-art devices that have wider coverage in terms of monitoring and alerting, which benefits responsiveness to emergency management and public safety officials, and builds public trust, equity and confidence. (q) Recognized Volunteer Groups (RVG) - are volunteer groups not included under the definition of ACDVs but are recognized by the City Government of Davao or LDRRMC. (r) Reconstruction - the medium- and long-term rebuilding and sustainable restoration of resilient critical infrastructures, services, housing, facilities and livelihoods required for the ful! functioning of a community or a society affected by a disaster, aligning with the principles of sustainable development and "build back better," to avoid or reduce future disaster risk. (s) Recovery - the restoring or improving of livelihoods and health, as well as economic, physical, social, cultural and environmental assets, systems and activities, of a disaster-affected community or society, aligning with the principles of sustainable development and "build back betteri' to avoid or reduce future disaster risk. (t) Rehabilitation - the restoration of basic seruices and facilities for the functioning of a community or a society affected by a disaster. (u) Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) - a standard operating procedure is a set of step-by-step instructions compiled by an organization to help workers carry out routine operations. SOPs aim to achieve efficiency, quality output, and uniformity of peformance while reducing miscommunication and failure to comply with the organization's regulations. (v) Vulnerable Groups - include individuals or groups of people that face higher exposure to disaster risk and povefi including, but not limited to, women, especially pregnant and lactating mothers, children and youth, especially orphans and unaccompanied children, elderly, differently-abled people, and people with chronic illnesses.

text: EVACUATION - The following protocols shall be obserued in the implementation of preemptive evacuation : (a) Upon the assessment and monitoring relative to imminent danger caused by weather disturbance and other hazards, the CDRRMO-Operation Center through the Head of Office shal! immediately inform the City Mayor and seek clearance for the implementation of evacuation procedures and protocols. On the basis of such recommendation, the City Mayor shall immediately declare the implementation and enforcement of preemptive evacuation, which shall be guided by the following factors: i. Conditions for Evacuation; ii. Chain of Command; iii. Evacuation Procedures; iv. Emergency Standards; and v. Early Warning System. (b)The Preemptive Evacuation shall be enforced in three different levels, as follows: i. Level 1 refers to a voluntary evacuation during Green Warning Signal; ii. Level 2 refers to the evacuation of vulnerable sectors, within four (4) hours, enforced during Yellow Warning Signal; and iii. Level 3 refers to complete evacuation, within four (4) hours, enforced during Orange and Red Warning Signal. Here, inhabitants or would-be disaster victims are mandated to evacuate in view of an imminent danger against their life. In cases where the inhabitants or would-be disaster victims refuse or resist to vacate, he or she may be forcibly taken if the situation warrants as a means of ensuring his or her safety. (c) If anyone within the affected area does not adhere to the order of evacuation during a Level 2 or Level 3 pre-emptive evacuation, the person may be compulsorily taken, if the situation warrants as a means of ensuring his or her safety; a Page 6 of t2 Ord. No. 0246-23 (d) CDRRMO shall mobilize all search and rescue teams not limited to BDRRIvICS, RVGs, ACDVS, and CVRS in accordance with the Clustering of Emergency Resources. SECTIOil 6. CONSIDERATION IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF EMERGENCY EVACUATIOI{ - These protocols shall be obserued in the implementation of emergency evacuations: (a) Emergency Evacuation is a full evacuation of all residents and occupants within the hazard or disaster area and will be resofted to in cases where the forecasted impact of the hazard or disaster is within less than two (2) hours or in any incidents that are about to occur, are already occurring, or have already occurred, such as in the case of fire, eafthquake, terrorist attack or criminal activity within an area; (b) Emergency Evacuation shall be carried out in a manner that is humane, respectful of the dignity of a person, not using disproportionate force, without discrimination and with conscious attention to the needs of vulnerable sectors, prioritizing children, pregnant women, the elderly, Persons With Disabilities (PWDs) and those with chronic illnesses; (c) Personnel and volunteers carrying out the emergency evacuation shall make sure that al! measures are taken to inform the evacuees, in a manner and language that they can understand, of the need for a hasty and orderly evacuation, and the lack of other alternatives for their evacuation. text: ESTABLISHMENT OF EVACUATION SITES AT THE COMMUNITY TEVEL -There shall be established evacuation sites, both Permanent and Alternative, to be utilized by the affected area/s during hazards or disasters: (a) Permanent Evacuation Sites - There shall be an established permanent evacuation site per barangay as evaluated and designated by the CDRRMO in coordination with the BDRRMC, to serue as shelter for people in times of calamities and emergencies. text: RETURN, REHABILITATION, AND RECONSTRUCTION (RRR) - The CDRRMO, together with the BDRRMC, and other concerned agencies, shall implement the fol lowi n g post-d isaster/post-emergency g u idel i nes : (a) Return - Provided that the affected area is not or has not been declared a "No Build Zone," "High Risk Arear" "Danger Zone," or "Hazard Prone Area," after the disaster or hazard, a notice shal! be issued by the City Mayor when the disaster or hazard has already subsided, that the affected areas are declared safe for habitation and for the IDPs to return to the said areas. text: - The following are the general duties and obligations of the City Government of Davao as a Personal Information Controller (PIC): A. Personal data shall be processed for purposes of facilitating the peformance of iE public functions and the provision of public seruices pursuant to its mandate. In all instances, it shall adhere to the general data privacy principles of transparency, legitimate purpose, and proportionality; B. Reasonable and appropriate safeguards shall be implemented for the protection of persona! data of data subjects of the CITY GOVERNMENT OF DAVAO, whether internal (officials, employees, job order, contract of service, casual, etc.) or external (clients, visitors, other stakeholders, etc.); C. The rights of the data subjects shall be upheld, subject to limitations as may be provided for by law. The free exercise of applicable rights shall be enabled through mechanisms that are clear, simple, straightforward, and convenient for the data subjects; and D. The data privacy rights of the affected data subjects shall be harmonized with the right to information on matters of public concern. It is recognized that both rights are imperative for transparenf, accountable, and pafticipatory governance, and are key factors for effective and reasonable public pafticipation in social, poliUcal, and economic decision-making. SECTIOI{ 5. SPECIFIC COMPLIAI{CE REQUIREMENTS. - The tullowing specific compliance requirements under the DPA, ib IRR as amended, and relevant issuances of the National Privacy Commission (NPC), are hereby set out as follows: A. Desionati6n of Persons Responsible- Pursuant to SECTION 2l of the DP& PIG shall designate individual/s who shall facilitate and ensure the PIC's responsibility and accountability for the organization's compliance with the DPA. The following are hereby designated: A.1. Data Protection Officer (DPO)-The City Mayor shall designate the DPO, through a memorandum, tasked with the duties and responsibilities of ensuring the compliance of the City Government of Davao with the DPA, its IRR, and other NPC issuances. I rt Ord. No. 0258-23 It shall have the following functions: a. Monitor the Personal Information Controllers (PICs) or Personal Information Processors (PIPs) compliance with the Data Privacy Act (DPA), its Implementing Rules & Regulations (IRR), issuances by the National Privacy Commission (NPC) and other applicable laws and policies. For this purpose, he or she may: i. Collect information to identiff the processing operations, activities, measures, prcjects, programs, or systems of the PIC or PIP, and maintain a record thereof; ii. Analpe and check the compliance of processing activities, including the issuance of security clearances and compliance by third-pafi seryice providerc; iii. Inform, advise, and issue recommendations to the PIC or PIP; iv. Asceftain renewal of accreditations or ceftifications necessary to maintain the required standards in perconal data processing; and v. Advise the PIC or PIP as regards the necessity of executing a Data Sharing Agreement with third parties, and ensure its compliance with law. b. Ensure the conduct of Privary Impact Assessments (PIA) relative to activities, measures, projects, programs, or systems of the PIC or PIP; c. Advise the PIC or PIP regarding complaints and/or the exercise by data subjects of their rights (e.9,, requests for information, clarifications, rectification, or deletion of personal data); d. Ensure proper data breach and security incident management by the PIC or PIP, including the latter's preparation and submission to the NPC of repofts and other documentation concerning security incidents or data breaches within the prescribed period; e. Inform and cultivate awareness on privacy and data protection within the organization of the PIC or PIP, including al! relevant laws, rules and regulations and issuances of the NPC; f. Advocate for the development review and /or revision of policies, guidelines, projects and/or programs of the PIC or PIP relating to privacy and data protection, by adopting a privacy by design approach; g. Serue as the contact person of the PIC or PIP vis-i-vis data subjects, the NPC and other authorities in all matters concerning data privacy, security issues or concerns of the PIC or PIP; , Ord. No.0258-23 Cooperate, coordinate, and seek the advice of the NPC regarding matters concerning data privary and security; Perform other duties and tasks that may be assigned by the PIC or PIP that will further the interest of data privacy and security and uphold the rights of the data subjects; The DPO or his or her authorized representative/s shall create the necessary user accounts in the applicable NPC system/s in compliance of the requirements for registration and personal data breach notification and management; The contact details of the DPO should be made available and easily accessible on the official website and social media page/s and should include the following infomration: a. Title or designation- the name of the DPO need not be published but should be made available upon request by a data subject: b. Postal address: and c. Dedicated telephone number and email address. The designated DPO shall be assisted by Compliance Officers for Privacy (COPs) and Data Privacy Committee created herein. A.2 -There shall be a Compliance Officer for Privary (COP) per office, one (1) primary and one (1) alternate, who must be a Plantilla personnel, and duly covered by a memorandum from the Human Resource Management Office. Functions: 1. Repoft to the DPO any data breach and security incident within the prescribed period; 2. Inform and cultivate awareness on privacy and data protection within their respective offices; 3. Suggest to the DPO the development, review and/or revision of policies, guidelines, projects and/or programs of the PIC or PIP relating to privacy and data protection; 4. Serue as the focal person of their respective offices in all matters concerning data privacy or security issues; and 5. Peform other duties and tasks that may be assigned by the DPO that will fufther the interest of data privacy and security and uphold the rights of the data subjects. h i. j k. Ord. No. 0258-23 A.3 Data Privaor Committee-The Data Privary Committee (herein after referred to as the "Committee" for brevity) shall be primarily composed of the duly appointed representatives of the following offices: Chairpercon: City Mayor's Office Vice Chairpercon: City Legal Office Members: . City Administrator's Office . City Information and Technology Center . City Archives and Records Office . City Civil Registrar's Office . SANGGUNIANG Panlungsod, Committee on Information Technology . Human Resource Management Office . City Social Welfare and Development Office . City Health Office The City Mayor may, through an Executive Order, add additiona! members to the Committee, as may be deemed necessary. The members of the Data Privacy Committee shall perform functions as may be instructed by the City Mayor and/or the DPO, such as but not limited to, reviewing contracts involving processing of personal data and provide technical advice to the DPO based on their areas of expeftise. The presence of a simple majority of all the members of the Committee shall constitute a quorum. B. Conduct of Privaor Impact Assessment- AII departments and offices as process ownerc shall conduct a Privary Impact Assessment (PIA) on any personal data processing system prior to their adoption, use, or implementation. 1. For existing systems, the DPO shal! be consulted by the respective process owners on the appropriateness of conducting a PIA and the reasonable timeframe to accomplish the same; 2. For both existing and proposed systems, there may be a determination that the conduct of a PIA is not necessary if the processing involves minimal risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects, taking into account the recommendations from the DPO. In making this determination, the following should be considered: a. Size and sensitivity of the personal data being processed; b. Duration and extent of processing; c. Likely impact of the processing to the life of the data subjecU and d. Possible harm in case of a personal data breach; Ord. No.0258-23 3. The conduct of a PIA may be outsourced to a third-party service provider, as may be recommended by the DPO, subject to the laws, rules, and regulations applicable to government procurement; 4. The relevant issuances and other information, education, and communication materials of the Nrc or PIA and other relevant issuances shall serue as additional guidance; and 5. The results of the PIA conducted shall be made the basis for the preparation of the Privacy Management Program, the Privary Manual, and the crafting of the appropriate privary notices specific to the personal data processing activities being undertaken by the pertinent deparfirents and offices and other applicable policies relevant to data .privacy and security. C. Adootion of a Privacy Manaoement Prooram and Privacy ManualThe City Government of Davao shall prepare a Privacy Management Program, which shall contain, among others, the necessary policies and processes that remediates the gaps identified in the PIA and a Privacy Manual, as may be supplemented by the existing or prospective codes, guides, manuals, privacy notices, ordinances, policies and other documented information on processes that may deal with any data privacy matter. 1. The DPO, the Committee, and the COPs shall be tasked to ensure that all relevant records and other documentation on data privacy are maintained and kept up to date; and 2. The Privary Management Program and Privacy Manual shall be subject to regular review, evaluation, and updating, where appropriate, considering the best practices and national and/or international standards for data privary and security. D. Implementation of SecuriW Measures - Reasonable and appropriate organizational, technical, and physical security measures shall be implementgd by all departrnents and offices processing personal data. 1. The determination of what is reasonable and appropriate shall take into account the following factors as determined following the PIA conducted: a. Nature and volume of the personal data to be protected; b. Risk of the processing to the involved data subjects; c. Size of the department or office and complexity of its persona! data processing activities; d. Current data privacy best practices; and e. Cost of implementation. Ord. No.0258-23 2. The security measures to be implemented shall ensure the protection of personal data against any unlawful processing and the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the personal data being processed. The DPO, in consultation and coordination with the City Information and Technology Center, in the case of digibl-based or electronic systems, and the City Archives and Records Office, in the case of paper-based documents, shall make the appropriate determination and recommendation on the measures and policies to be implemented. These may include back-up solutions, access controls, secure log files, acceptable use, encryption and data disposal mechanisms, among others, for any personal data processing activity. 3. The data sharing and outsourcing arrangements shall be subject to the execution of the appropriate agreements as may be determined by the Committee in consultation with the DPO. For this purpose, the relevant issuances of the NPC shall be obserued accordingly. E. Security Incident Manaoement: Perconal Data Breach Manaoement - The following policies and procedures are set out for purposes of managing security incidents, including personal data breaches. 1. Data Breach Response Team (DBRT)- A data breach response team is hereby created with the following members: the DPO and the Data Privacy Committee. The DBRT shall be responsible for the following actions: a. Assess and evaluate all security incidents, including personal data breaches; b. Restore integrity to the affected information and communications systems; c. Recommend measures for mitigation and remedies on any resulting damage to the CITY GOVERNMENT OF DAVAO and the affected data subjects; d. Comply with the mandatory notification and other repofting requirements indicated in the appropriate NPC issuance; and e. Coordinate with the appropriate government Computer Emergenry Response Team (CERT) and law enforcement agencies, where appropriate. 2. Incident Response Procedure - The DBRT shall recommend the actual procedure or manual for the timely discovery and management of security incidents. This shall include: a. Identification of person/s responsible for regular monitoring and evaluation of security incidents; b. Reporting lines in the event of a personal data breach; Ord. No. 0258-23 c. Evaluation of the security incidents or personal data breaches as to its nature, extent and cause, the adequacy of safeguards in place, immediate and long-term impact of the personal data breach, and its actual and potential harm and negative consequences to affected data subjects; d. Procedures for contacting law enforcement if necessary; e. Conduct of investigations on the security incident, including personal data breaches; f. Procedures for notiffing the NPC and data subjects when the personal data breach is subject to mandatory notification requirements; g. Procedures in assisting affected data subjects to mitigate the possible harm and negative consequences in the event of a personal data breach.

text: LEGAL BASIS - SECTION 2l of Republic Act No. 10121 states that not less than five percent (5olo) of the estimated revenue from regular sources shall be set aside as Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (DLDRRMF) to suppoft disaster risk management activities such as, but not limited to, pre-disaster preparedness programs including training, purchasing life-saving rescue equipment, supplies and medicines, for post-disaster activities, and for the payment of premiums on calamity insurance. The same law likewise provides that, of the amount appropriated for LDRRMF, thity percent (30o/o) shall be allocated as Quick Response Fund (QRF) or stand-by fund for relief and recovery programs so that situation and living conditions of people in communities or areas stricken by disasters, calamities, epidemics, or complex emergencies, may be normalized as quickly as possible. Further, upon the recommendation of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (LDRRMO) and approval of the sanggunian concerned, the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (LDRRMC) may transfer the said fund to support disaster risk reduction work of other LDRRMCs which are declared under the state of calamity.

text: LEGAL BASIS - SECTION 2l of Republic Act No. t072L states that not less than five percent (5olo) of the estimated revenue from regular sources shall be set aside as Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) to suppoft disaster risk management activities such as, but not limited to, pre-disaster preparedness programs, including training, purchasing life-saving rescue equipment, supplies and medicines, for post-disaster activities, and for the payment of premiums on calamity insurance. The same law likewise provides that, of the amount appropriated for LDRRMF, thirty percent (30%) shall be allocated as Quick Response Fund (QRF) or stand-by fund for relief and recovery programs so that situations and living conditions of people in communities or areas stricken by disasters, calamities, epidemics, or complex emergencies, may be normalized as quickly as possible. Further, upon the recommendation of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (LDRRMO) and approval of the sanggunian concerned, the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (LDRRMC) may transfer the said fund to support disaster risk reduction work of other LDRRMCs which are declared under a State of Calamity.

text: - Pursuant to SECTION 2 of Republic Act No. 9729 or the "Climate Change Act of 2009" as amended by Republic Act No. L0174, the City Government of Davao hereby declares the following as its policies: 1. The Local Government shall afford full protection and advancement of the right of all Dabawenyos to a healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature; 2. The Local Government shall enjoin the pafticipation of national and local governments, businesses, non-government organizations, local communities and the public to prevent and reduce the adverse impacts of climate change and, at the same time, maximize the potential benefits of climate change; 3. It shall also be the policy of the Local Government to strengthen, integrate, consolidate and institutionalize government initiatives to achieve coordination in the implementation of plans and programs to address climate change in the context of sustainable development; 4. The Local Government recognizes that climate change and disaster risk reduction and management are closely interrelated and effective. Disaster risk reduction and management will enhance adaptive capacity to climate change. In consonance with this, the Local Government shall integrate disaster risk reduction into climate change programs and initiatives; 5. Finally, the Local Government shall embrace a systematic concept of climate change in various phases of policy formulation, development plans, povefi reduction strategies and other development tools and techniques by all agencies and instrumentalities of the government.

In establishing an operationa! inpatient shelter facility for Indigenous Peoples and Muslims (IPs/Muslims), the following are considerable objectives to prioritize the well-being, cultural sensitivity, and specific needs of this community: 1. Ensure that the facility respects and incorporates Indigenous cultural practices, traditions, and languages to create a culturally safe and welcoming environment; 2. Provide access to healthcare seruices that are sensitive to the unique health challenges faced by Indigenous Cultural Communities (ICCs), including addressing issues related to historical trauma and disparities in healthcare access by offering a range of seruices that address not only physical health but also mental, emotional, and spiritual wellbeing, reflecting indigenous concepts of holistic health; 3. Implement trauma-informed care principles to create a safe and suppottive environment for Indigenous and Muslim individuals who may have experienced historical or personal trauma by providing counselling seruices that is culturally relevant to the individuals seeking help; 4. Involve Indigenous and Muslim community members in the planning, operation, and decision-making processes to ensure that the facility meets their specific needs and preferences; 5. Collaborate with Indigenous and Muslim-led organizations and tribal authorities to strengthen the network of support and resources available to the community; 6. Ensure that the facility's physical environment, design, and artwork are culturally appropriate and reflect Indigenous and Muslim aesthetics and values; Ord. No. 0429-24 7. Develop a sustainable operational and funding plan that ensures the facility's long-term existence and effectiveness in meeting the needs of Indigenous and Muslim individuals; and 8. To supplement other government seruices to the eleven (11) major tribes not mentioned in this Ordinance.

Food; o Medicines and other medical supplies; . Cash Assistance not exceeding Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000.00) per household for immediate household needs. text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - As used in this Ordinance, the following terms and phrases shall mean as follows: 1. City Government - refers to the City Government of Davao. 2. Geodiversity - the natural range or diversity of geological features (rocks, minerals, fossils, structures), geomorphological features (landforms and processes), soil and water that compose and shape the physical landscape. It is not usually defined to inctude landscaping, concrete, or other human landforms and products. 3. Geological heritage (geoheritage) - a generic but descriptive term applied to sites or areas of geologic features with significant scientific, educational, cultural, or aesthetic value. Ord. No. 0464-24 4. Geoparks- are places where landscapes with outstanding geological heritage are used to suppoft sustainable development. This is achieved through conseryation, education, inlerpersonal and naturebased tourism. 5. National Integrated Protected Areas System (NIPAS) the classification and administration of all designated protected areas to maintain essential ecological processes and life-support systems, to preserue genetic diversity, to ensure sustainable use of resources found therein, and to maintain their natural conditions to the greatest extend possible. 6. Natural park - a relatively large area not materially altered by human activity where extractive resources uses are not allowed and is maintained to protect outstanding natural and scenic areas of national or international significance for scientific, educational, and recreational use. 7. Protected area - identified portions of land and/or water set aside by reason of their unique physical and biological diversity and protected against destructive human exploitation. 8. UNESCO Global Geoparks (UGGp) - single, unified geographical areas where sites and landscapes of internationa! geological significance are managed with a holistic concept of protection, education and sustaina ble development. sEcTroN 5. MANAGEMENT oF MOUNT APo GEOPARK - The Mount Apo Geopark shall be managed pursuant to Republic Act 11038 and Republic Act 9237 or the Mount Apo Act of 2003. UNESCO Global Geoparks are managed by a Body having legal existence recognized under national legislation. This management body should be appropriately equipped to address the entire area and should include all relevant local and regional actors and authorities. UNESCO Global Geoparks require a management plan, agreed upon by all the paftners, that provides for the social and economic needs of the local populations, protects the landscape in which they live and conserues their cultural identity. The plan must be comprehensive, incorporating the governance, development, communication, protection, infrastructure, finances and partnerships of the UNESCO Global Geopark. DENR Region XI shall be the primary agency to manage the Mount Apo Geopark (Davao City side), in close coordination with the Loca! Government Unit (LGU)-Davao City and other concerned organizations/groups. The Regional Director may enter into a Memorandum of Agreement (MoA)/Partnership Agreement with the concerned LGU, and peoples Organizations.

text: DECIARATION OF POUCY- Pursuant to Republic Act (R.A.) No. 7160 (Local Government Code of 1991), the City Government of Davao shall exercise the powers expressly granted, those necessarily implied therefrom, as well as powers necessary, appropriate, or incidental for its efficient and effective governance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare. Within its respective territorial jurisdiction, it shall ensure and support the maintenance of peace and order, and the preseruation of the comfort and convenience of its inhabitants. Thus, it is the Poliry of the City Government of Davao to ensure the prevention, suppression, and imposition of proper penalties for smoking, vaping, or engaging in similar activities in public places, selling the same to minors or allowing them to engage in such activities and such other acts using the same that are inimica! to the heatth and welfare of the inhabitants of the City.

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - For purposes of this Ordinance, the following terms are defined operationally: 1. Accommodation and Enteftainment Establishments - refer to establishments that provide food, accommodation, drinks, merchandise, entertainment or other professional seruices, including but not limited to, restaurants, fast foods, eateries, hotels, motels, lodges, inns, boarding houses, disco houses, videoke bars, resto bars, and movie houses, or any other place with pleasant environment and atmosphere conducive to comfoft, healthful relaxation and rest, offering food and/or drinks, sleeping accommodation and recreation facilities to the public for a fee; 2. Centers of Youth Activities - refer to places such as playschools, preparatory schools, elementary schools, high schools, colleges and universities, youth hostels, parks and playgrounds, and other recreational facilities for minors; 3. Children Rescued - refer to minors rescued from any conceivable forms of danger, including substance use and abuse; 4. Electronic Device Systems (EDS) - refer to any device, such as electronic nicotine device system, electronic cigarette, vapes and other similar devices, whether or not it is used to deliver nicotine to the user, that resembles the outward appearance of real smoking products; 5. Enclosed or Paftially Enclosed Public Place - refers to all places, which are enclosed by one or more walls or sides, whether covered by a roof or not, or even if open on all sides but is covered by a roof, regardless of whether the structure is permanent or temporary in nature, that are accessible or open to the public, whether or not by invitation or by payment, or all places for collective use, regardless of ownership or right to access including, but not limited to, gasoline stations, banks, malls, shopping/business arcades, town squares, terminals, airpoft, seaports, schools, places of worship/churches, hospitals, cinema houses, gymnasiums/covered courts, funeral parlors, barber shops, cockpits, gaming Page 3 of t4 Ord. No. 0472-24 areas, recreational facilities, pedestrian overpass, indoor car parks, waiting sheds, sidewalks, and other places where people usually congregate; 6. Immediately Dangerous to Life or Health (IDLH) - describes hazards in which an acute exposure to the hazard poses a severe risk of immediate health damage, injury, or death. This is determined by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) or the City Health Office (CHO), with proper coordination with the FDA, in accordance with their existing policies and standards; 7. Minors - are persons who are below the age of majority or below the legal age of eighteen (18) years, or persons who are eighteen (18) years of age or older, but are incapable of taking care of themselves due to their mental incapacity; 8. Person-in-charge - refers to the president/manager, in case of a company, corporation, paftnership or association, the owner/proprietor/operator, in case of a single proprietorship, of accommodation and entertainment establishments, whether tourism-accredited or not, or the administrator in case of government or private propefi, facility, office or building, workplaces, enclosed or paftially enclosed public places, public buildings, public outdoor spaces, places of worship, hazardous areas, food preparation areas, health facilities of any kind, centers of youth activity or other facilities frequented particularly by minors, and the city/municipal schools superintendent, school president, dean or principal, in case of schools; 9. Public Conveyances - refer to any vehicle, whether mobile or stationary, used in the transpoft of passengers or available to the public as a mode of transport, such ds, but not limited to, jeepneys, buses, trains, vans, taxis, airplanes, ships, and other modes of water transpoftation, trirycles, motorcycles, and other public utility vehicles whether covered by a Certiflcate of Public Convenience or not; 10. Public Building - refers to any of the following: A building or structure owned by the government or owned by a private person but used, rented, or occupied by the government or any of its instrumentalities; or Any building or structure used or controlled exclusively for public purposes by any depaftment or branch of government, local government unit, or barangay without reference to the ownership of the building; 11. Public Outdoor Spaces - refer to outdoor spaces that are open to the public or places where facilities are available for the public or where a crowd of people gather or congregate or regardless of ownership or right to access such as, but not limited to, parks, playgrounds, spofts grounds or centers, gaming areas, gardens, resorts, beaches, pools, markets, streets, sidewalks, parking areas, walkways, entrance ways, waiting areas, stairwells and the like' 12. Shisha - refers to a device or instrument which may have a single or multistemmed pipe for smoking, whether or not it delivers nicotine to the user, in which the smoke is passed through a water basin before inhalation. It is also known as water pipe, Sheesha, Hookah, Nergeela, Argeel and Nargile; a I Page 4 of L4 Ord. No. 0472-24 13. Smoking/Vaping - refers to the lighting and/or puffing of any cigarette, cigar, tobacco product of any kind, form or type, EDS, Shisha, vape and the like, whether it contains nicotine or not. Possession of any lighted and/or puffed cigarette, cigar or any tobacco product, or an actually operated EDS, Shisha, Vape and the like within the prohibited areas for smoking shall constitute "prima facid'evidence of smoking/vaping as prohibited under this ordinance; 14. Tobacco Product - any product that consists of loose tobacco, whether or not it contains nicotine, and is intended for use in a cigarette, including any product containing tobacco, and intended for smoking/vaping or oral or nasal use; and 15. workplaces - an area, permanent or temporary, in which a person performs duties of employment or work, regardless of whether the work is done for compensation or on a voluntary basis, and includes private offices, common area and any other area which is generally used or frequented during the course of employment or work. Company-owned vehicles used for transpofting employees and guests or any vehicle used in the course of work are considered workplaces.

text: COVERAGE - It shall be unlawful for any person to smoke/vape or allow the smoking/vaping of any tobacco product, or use EDS, Shisha, Vape and the like, in all forms of Public Conveyances, Government-owned Vehicles, Accommodation and Enteftainment Establishments, Workplaces, Enclosed or Partially Enclosed Public Places, Public Buildings and Public Outdoor Spaces, Places of Worship, Hazardous Areas, Food Preparation Areas, Health Facilities of any kind, Centers of Youth Activities, and areas within one hundred (100) meters from any point of the perimeter of Schoots, Public Playgrounds or other facilities frequented particularly by minors, except in duly designated smoking/vaping areas as deflned in SECTION 5 hereunder, within the territorial jurisdiction of Davao City. It shall also be unlawful for any person to domestically manufacture or adulterate any tobacco product, EDS, Shisha, Vape and the like that are IDLH. It shall also be unlawful for any person, natural or juridical, to direct, order, compel, request or ask a minor to acquire or purchase from, possess, sell, offer or distribute any tobacco product, EDS, Shisha, Vape and the like, to any other person and/or for any other person, and to allow, abet, tolerate or permit such minor to acquire, purchase, possess, sell, offer, distribute, use, consume, or smoke/vape any tobacco product, EDS, Shisha, Vape, and the like.

text: DESIGNATED SMOKING/VAPING AREA (DSVA) - refers to an outdoor space where a person is permitted to smoke and vape without violating this Ordinance, provided that, the same meets the following requirements, at the minimum: There shall be no opening that will allow air to escape from the DSVA to the smoke/vape-free area of the building or conveyance, except for a single door equipped with an automatic door closer; It shall be located in or within ten (10) meters from entrances, exits, or any place where people pass or congregate, or in front of air intake ducts; Page 5 of t4 Ord. No. 0472-24 The DSVA shall not be larger than twenty percent (20o/o) of the total floor area of the building or conveyance, provided that, in no case shall such area be larger than five (5) square meters; No building or conveyance shall have more than one DSVA; Provided that, persons-in-charge have the option of establishing one (1) Designated Smoking Area (DSA) and one (1) Designated Vaping Area (DVA) therein, subject to the same standards under this SECTION, with a combined area not exceeding twenty percent (20o/o) of the total floor area of the building or conveyance; Minors shall not be allowed inside the DSVA; It shall have the following signages highly visible and prominently displayed: a. "Smoking/Vaping Area" signage; b. Graphic health warnings on the effects of using tobacco products, EDS, Shisha, Vape and the like; and c. Prohibition on the entry of minors, pregnant women, and lactating mothers. vil Other standards and specifications to better ensure a smoke/vape-free environment as may be prescribed by existing laws, rules and regulations and policies; Provided that, such standards and specifications are consistent with this Ordinance and that persons-in-charge are given sixty (60) days to comply upon the effectivity of this Ordinance. Nothing in this Ordinance shall compel persons-in-charge to establish DSVAs nor prevent them from instituting more stringent measures in their buildings and establishments to better ensure a smoke/vape-free environment in their premises. All DSVAs shall be covered by a Ceftificate of Compliance from the City Mayort Office through the Anti-Vices Task Force (AWF), created under this Ordinance.

The citation ticket shall state, among others, the name and address of the violator, the specific violation committed, and the corresponding administrative penalty. There shall be three (3) copies of the citation ticket - the fiist copy shall be endorsed to the VRU, the second copy shall be given to the violator, and the third copy shall be retained by the apprehending enforcer. Failure to pay any of the administrative fines per count shall result in an additional administrative fine of One Hundred Pesos (P100.00) a day per count; provided, that the total amount of administrative flne per count shall not exceed Five Thousand pesos (P5,000.00); Provided, fufther, that non-payment of the total administrative fines per count within three (3) working days from the time of apprehension or issuance of citation ticket or failure to undergo the mandated smoking/vaping cessation counseling shall lead to the prosecution of the case in court, subject to the penalties provided herein, without prejudice to the prosecution of other actions.
title: Ordinance No. 0472-24

text: DEPUTIZED ENFORCERS - The City Mayor, through the Vices Regulation Unit (VRU), may deputize and authorize representatives from Davab City police Office (DCPO) to issue the corresponding citation tickets, and apprehend violators, and the same shall be responsible in the strict implementation of this Ordinance. Barangay officials or representatives from PSSO - Civi! Security Unit (CSU), Business Bureau, City Economic Enterprise (CEE), City Health Office (CHO), City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO), private sector, non-government organizations, and government organizations may also be deputized and authorized to monitor compliance with the provisions of this Ordinance and repoft violations to the proper apprehending officers.
title: Ordinance No. 0472-24

text: TRAINING AND DEPUTA,TION - All deputized enforcers shall be required to undergo training on enforcement before they are deputized and allowed to enforce this Ordinance. Only those who shall complete and pass the training shall be deputized as enforcers by the City Mayor.
title: Ordinance No. 0472-24

text: BARANGAY OFFICIALS - Barangay Officials in Davao City shall assist with the information dissemination on the salient features of this Ordinance, and shall properly coordinate with the Depaftment of Education XI (DepEd XI), the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) XI, Technical Education and Skills Development Ord. No. 0472-24 Authority XI (TESDA XI), Business Bureau, Davao City Police Office (DCPO), Vices Regulation Unit (VRU), Public Safety and Security Office (PSSO), Civil Security Unit (CSU), City Economic Enterprise (CEE), City Health Office (CHO) and/or City Social Wetfare and Development Office (CSWDO) in strictly enforcing the provisions herein within the respective territorial jurisdiction of their Barangays. Barangay Officials shall immediately coordinate with DCPO and/or CSWDO and ensure the rescue of minors whenever they are involved in the possession, sale, acquisition, distribution, utilization, consumption of, or engaged in any transaction involving any tobacco product, EDS, Shisha, Vape, and the like. text: REVIEW OF ANTI-SMOKING ORDINANCE - The VRU shall conduct a review of the provisions provided in this Ordinance every five (5) years, or whenever the agenry deems it necessary to amend the provisions provided in this Ordinance, to ensure the relevance, and appropriateness of the regulations and submit the same to the SANGGUNIANG Panlungsod, for amendment.

text: INFORMATION. EDUCATION, AND COMMUNICATION CAMPAIGN - There shall be a Public Information Drive regarding the implementation of this Ordinance and it shall be headed by the City Information Office (CIO) in close coordination with the Department of Education XI (DepEd XI), the Commission on Higher Education XI (CHED XI), Technical Education and Skills Development Authority XI OESDA XI), Business Bureau, Davao City Police Office (DCPO), Vices Regulation Unit (VRU), the Public Safety and Security Office (PSSO), the Civil Security Unit (CSU), the City Economic Enterprise (CEE), the City Health Office (CHO), the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO), and other enforcing and implementing agencies. Information dissemination through signages, flyers, audio-visual presentations, and other forms of public information dissemination shall be established.
title: Ordinance No. 0472-24

text: IMPLEMENTING RULES AND REGULATIONS (IRR) - The VRU shall promulgate such rules and regulations, with the approval of the City Mayor, as are necessary to ensure the effective implementation of this ordinance. Republic Act No. 10533 - otherwise known as "An Act Enhancing the Philippine Basic Education System by Strengthening its Curriculum and Increasing the Number of Years for Basic Education and Appropriating Funds Therefor and Other Purposes" in SECTION 5. (h) Curriculum Development states that "The DepEd shall formulate the design and details of the enhanced basic education curriculum. The curriculum shall be flexible enough to enable and allow schools to localize, indigenize and enhance the same based on their respective educational and social contexts. The production and development of locally produced teaching materials shall be encouraged and approval of these materials shall devolve to the regional and division education units". Likewise, the City Government of Davao aims to ensure that the people of Davao are empowered, protected, secure, gender and culturally sensitive to attain the best quality of life. Davao City aims to cultivate a disciplined and law-abiding citizenry, starting from the youngest member of society.

text: OBJECTIVES The objectives of this Ordinance are as follows: a. To develop among children and the youth an authentic appreciation of their sense of moral responsibility to their fellow citizens, democratic institutions, and human society. b. To empower the children and youth as future adults for them to understand, protect and help promote the common good as law-abiding citizens through self-discipline. c. To enable the children and youth to understand, reflect, and fully discern the role that social media and modern technology play in their lives. d. To guide the children and youth in realizing their duties as stewards of the environment and the good of the future generation. e. To form the children and youth into individuals who do not discriminate against others, especially the poor, and respect women, the elderly, Indigenous Peoples and the LGBTQ community. Ord. title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTING JANUARY AS BIBLE MONTH IN DAVAO CITY

text: - It is the policy of Davao City to recognize and celebrate the cultural and spiritual heritage of its people. In support of this commitment, Davao City hereby declares the month of January as Bible Month, an annual obseruance promoting the teachings, values, and wisdom of the Bible as paft of Davao's cultural and moral development.
title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTING JANUARY AS BIBLE MONTH IN DAVAO CITY

text: @IElgre - The objectives of this Ordinance are as follows: a) To encourage reflection on the teachings of the Bible and its relevance in promoting peace, unity, and moral integrity in Davao City; b) To promote intefaith understanding and respect for religious diversity within the City; and c) To inspire community engagement through organized activities that honor the Bible and encourage values formation across all sectors.
title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTING JANUARY AS BIBLE MONTH IN DAVAO CITY

text: BIBLE MONTH ACTMTIES - During the Bible Month, the following activities are encouraged across Davao City: 1. Local Bible-believing institutions/organizations and schools shall be encouraged to hold special Bible studies, youth programs, and familycentered activities that emphasize values formation; 2. The City Government, in paftnership with the private sector, Biblebelieving institutions/organizations, and NGOs, shall coordinate citywide events such as Bible exhibits, poster-making contests, seminars, and reflections that promote unity, moral values and other activities; 3. All Barangay Councils in Davao City are encouraged to suppoft and participate in Bible Month activities to foster a spirit of community, love and seruice.
title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTING JANUARY AS BIBLE MONTH IN DAVAO CITY

text: - The implementation of this Ordinance shall be under the Office of the City Mayor through the Moral Recovery Council, in coordination with the National Bible Month Ecumenical Team. These agencies shall encourage collaboration among educational, cultural, and Biblebelieving institutions/organizations to ensure the effective obseruance of the Bible Month.
title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTING JANUARY AS BIBLE MONTH IN DAVAO CITY

text: FUNDING - Funds shall be allocated for the effective implementation of this Ordinance and subsequent annual budget shall be necessary subject to the accounting rules and regulations. Ord. No. 07t7-24
