text: - The following are hereby declared policies of the City: a. To promote, improve, and safeguard the Panigan-Tamugan Watershed as the main suface water source of the City's drinking water and is the largest source of the City's suface water supply; b. To effectively manage and protect the physical, biological, and socio-economic attributes of the Panigan-Tamugan Watershed based on the assessment study based on the masterplan as specified under SECTION 4 therein; c. To ensure the Panigan-Tamugan Watershed's cleanliness, sustainable ecological balance, rich biodiversity, and improve the quality of life of the community; and d. To recognize that the watershed area is a recharged area for the City's aquifers which are sources of the City's drinking water that must be protected, conserved, maintained, and managed for the continued and full enjoyment of the present and future generations. sEcTIoN3.rc.Forthepurposeofthisordinance,the following terms are defined as follows: a. "Critical Waterched" pertains to areas of land which show critical degradation as to threaten their natural feature on which rainwater drains from a river system to a common outlet such as a dam, lake or sea; or areas where rain from a higher level of land flows down to a river, or stream then to the Davao Gulf; or a topographically delineated area of land from which rainwater can drain as sufface run-off via a specific river or stream system to a common outlet point, which may be a dam, irrigation system or a municipal water supply take-off point, or where a river or stream discharges water into a larger river, stream or lake. b. "Customaty Laws" refer to a body of written and/or unwritten rules, usages, customs and practices traditionally and continually recognized, accepted and observed by respective ICCs/IPs; c. "Environmentally Critical Areas (ECA)" refer to those areas declared by law as nationa! parks, watershed reserves, wildlife preserves and sanctuaries and all other areas identified as such by Presidential Proclamation 2L46, specifically in Items B, 1-11. d. "Groundwater" refers to subsurface water that occurs beneath a water table in soils and rocks, or in geological formations. e. "Indigenous Cultural Communities/Indigenous Peoples (ICCs llPs)' refer to groups of people or homogenous societies identified under Republic Act No. 837L, or The Indigenous Peoples Rights Act (IPRA) of L99T" generally consisting of the Obu Manuvu and other tribes within the PTW. Page 3 of I Ord. No, 0742-25 t. "Motorized equipment" refers to any machine that uses or is activated by a motor, engine, or other power source. For the purpose of this Ordinance, motorized equipment shall refer to chainsaws, drilling machines, sawmills or pumping stations. g. "Open dump" refers to a disposal area wherein the solid wastes are indiscriminately thrown or disposed of without due planning and consideration for environmental and health standards (R.A. No. 9003). h. "Protected Areas" refer to identified portions of land and water set aside by reasons of their unique physical and biological significance, managed to enhance biological diversity and protected against destructive human exploitation. i. 'PUSAI(A" is the traditiona! Obu Manuvu practice of sanctiffing entities, living or non-living, as "precious" or "sacred" because it has become priceless, from the perspective of a family, clan, or tribe. j. "Settlement" refers to formal and informal communities or built-up residential areas where people prefer to live in and land areas classified, zoned or convefted for current or future residential or housing development purposes, including socialized housing zones for the homeless and underprivileged. k. "Suface Water" refers to waters (e.9., rivers, lakes, bays) which are open to the atmosphere and subject to surface runoff. l. "Tourism and Recreational Activities" refer to activities people do for fun and enjoyment which shal! refer to trekking or hiking, swimming, camping, mountain biking, running, canoeing, kayaking, rafting, tubing, for recreational purposes. m. *Waterched Areas" are areas of land which rainwater drains via a river system to a common outlet such as dam, lake or the sea; an area where rain from the highest point flows down to a river and ultimately to the Davao Gulf or a topographical delineated area of land from which rainwater can drain as suface run-off via a specific stream of river system to a common outlet point which may be a dam, irrigation system or municipal water supply take-off point, or where the stream or river discharges water into a larger river, stream or lake. n.
